Nurse booked after newborn’s thumb accidentally severed at Pindi's Holy Family Hospital. RAWALPINDI: A nurse was booked by police for mistakenly chopping off the thumb of a newborn baby girl in the nursery ward of Rawalpindi Holy Family Hospital. Police investigating the incident said efforts were underway to trace and investigate the accused nurse, who had not been available so far. They said the exact circumstances in which the child’s thumb was cut off would be known after the investigation. Qasir Mehmood, the father of the child and a resident of Hassan Abdal, lodged an FIR with New Town police, stating that his 23-day-old daughter had been admitted to the Holy Family Hospital’s nursery ward for treatment after being born at the hospital. He said that when he visited his daughter on Thursday evening, he found that her right thumb had been cut off. After he inquired from the doctor, he was told that a nurse had mistakenly cut off the child’s thumb during treatment in the nursery ward. The doctor informed him that the hospital would conduct an inquiry and let him know what had happened, he stated in the FIR. After the complaint was lodged, local police reached the hospital and later registered a case under the relevant section of the law. Meanwhile, the father of the newborn told Dawn on Friday that the nurse had joined the hospital’s inquiry and revealed the circumstances in which the child’s thumb was cut off. “I have forgiven her after she apologised,” he said. Separately, a Bykea rider was deprived of his motorcycle, cash and cell phone by three unidentified persons after reaching their destination in Ratta Amral. Usman Ali complained to the police that while carrying three passengers on his motorcycle near Mandi Mor, he was taken to a deserted place where one of the passengers held him at gunpoint and snatched his motorcycle, cell phone and Rs800. Police have registered a case and initiated an investigation into the incident. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

Karachi's DHA City becomes first private entity to light up its own housing project. ISLAMABAD: In a first, the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra) on Friday awarded DHA City, located on M-9 motorway, two parallel licences for electricity distribution and supplier of last resort (SoLR) for a period of 21 years. This is the first of its kind move under which a privately owned entity — DHA Energy Supply Company (Desco) — got licences to have both responsibilities of distribution of electricity and the supplier of last resort under the revised Nepra regime for competitive trading bilateral contract market (CTBCM) other than legacy utility distributors and SoLRs like ex-Wapda distribution companies and K-Electric. Initially, Desco’s jurisdiction for the distribution licence would be in DHA City Karachi (DHACK), located about 56 kilometres from Karachi city in district Malir. In its application, Desco reported that there was no infrastructure that may connect it to the national grid or KE network and the only source of supply available nearby was that of the Lucky Cement Limited with which it had reached an understanding for procurement of six megawatts (MW) of electricity and supply to residential, commercial and other consumers located in DHACK through KE. Nepra rejects objections of KE, Gepco and CPPA to grant distribution and SoLR licences to DHA Energy Supply Co. The state-owned Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) — the commercial arm of Power Division — Gujranwala Electric Supply Company (Gepco) and K-Electric (which has both these licences until June 2044 for entire Karachi, though non-exclusive after its monopoly ended in 2023) raised objections over the application of Desco. However, Nepra overruled the objections, saying the applicant had a case for consideration of the grant of distribution and SoLR licences. It issued the two licences strictly for its facilities located within DHACK. Desco shall charge a person availing distribution services only the tariff including use of system charges or connection charges with the approval of Nepra. While CPPA, Gepco and KE questioned the Desco’s requests on grounds of financial health, technical capabilities and proven track record, Nepra ruled that amendments to its Act envisaged introduction of reforms to liberalise the various segments of the supply chain of the electric power sector, including de-licensing of generation segment, allowing provincial grid companies in the transmission segment, carving out supply segment from the distribution (the wire business) and eliminating the exclusivity associated the with distribution segment of the supply chain. Also, the regulator ruled that being a relatively new company and not in actual operation, Desco “is not fulfilling this requirement at this moment however, at the same time its parent company — DHA Karachi — has strong financial credentials and shall bail out its special purpose vehicle whenever required”. It is also a common corporate practice to incorporate the company with minimum capital requirement of the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) and increase the paid up capital once the company commences its operations, it added. Moreover, the financial strength of the company was also expected to improve upon the grant of licences and commencement of its business which may not reasonably be achieved prior to undertaking the distribution/supply business in the first place, the regulator said, adding that the new company would now be under legal obligation to comply with all standards for which a special provision would be added in the standard terms and conditions of the distribution licence. ICC members vote to dismiss Karim Khan. THE HAGUE: Member states of the International Criminal Court voted on Friday to dismiss Karim Khan as prosecutor following allegations of sexual misconduct. Eighty-two of the court’s 125 member states voted in favour of the prosecutor’s removal. Khan, 56, denies any wrongdoing and his lawyer said he will challenge his dismissal. “Mr Khan will challenge the lawfulness and fairness of the decision through all available legal mechanisms,” lawyer Tayab Ali wrote on X. Khan’s dismissal follows an announcement by the United States that it will launch a renewed diplomatic campaign to dismantle the ICC, which it says is a threat to its sovereignty. Diplomats running the court’s oversight body decided last month that the British barrister had an inappropriate sexual relationship with a junior ICC lawyer and should be fired. Member states largely followed that conclusion in a vote at the United Nations in New York on Friday. During a visit to the Philippines on Thursday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there were “lunatics and crazies involved in the ICC” and there was no way any US political or military officials would ever go on trial at the court, reiterating previous criticism. The US, which is not a member, has imposed sanctions on 11 ICC judges and prosecutors, including Khan, citing the ICC’s arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defence Minister Yoav Gallant, and a past probe into US troops in Afghanistan. Khan’s accuser spoke publicly for the first time last week in an interview with CNN in which she repeated her allegations that the prosecutor had a non-consensual sexual relationship with her. Khan’s dismissal immediately triggers the election process for a new ICC prosecutor who is not expected to be voted in before next year. Any active ICC warrants will remain in place even after Karim Khan’s dismissal because only ICC judges have the authority to withdraw warrants. Published in Dawn, July 25th, 2026

Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia as Middle East conflict deepens. Houthi rebels claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia on Saturday, hours after vowing to retaliate against the kingdom for attacks as the Middle East conflict expanded. Riyadh struck Houthi military targets in Hodeida on Friday, with rebel media reporting two wounded after the Yemeni group announced a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hit its ships. The flare-up marks a new front of the war that has engulfed the region following US-Israeli strikes on Tehran in February, and comes on top of Iran’s parallel blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh’s only other maritime route. The rebels had accused Saudi Arabia of a “dangerous escalation” and said its actions “will not go unanswered”. The Houthis’ Ansarollah media said on Telegram early on Saturday that a “Yemeni missile strike” had sparked fires in the southern Saudi city of Jizan on the Red Sea. Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim. But Riyadh’s civil defence agency had issued brief warnings to residents in Jizan and Yanbu early Saturday for “potential danger”, only to lift the warnings minutes later. Similar warnings have been issued in the past when missiles or drones were fired at the kingdom. The warning came after the Saudi-led coalition said on Friday it had hit Houthi sites and destroyed targets threatening commercial vessels in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping. A Yemeni security source told AFP a naval base in the port city of Hodeida and a military camp on Kamaran island were among the Saudi targets. The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea. Blockade The Yemeni security source, who requested anonymity, said the Saudi strikes targeted a telecommunications building near Hodeida’s port and a naval base at Ras al-Kathib in Hodeida. The Houthis’ al-Masirah television channel said two people were wounded — a worker in Hodeida and a woman on Kamaran island. It said a telecoms building had been hit in Hodeida. On Monday, the rebels had warned in a radio message to ships that they would target vessels “belonging to (the) Saudi enemy” that do not comply with their blockade. Saudi state media cited a transport authority official on Friday as saying “the vessel (NCC MASA), belonging to a Saudi company, was targeted while sailing in the Red Sea today … resulting in minor damage to the vessel’s hull”. The ship resumed its course, the SPA added. Red Sea access has become vital for Saudi Arabia to keep shipping oil as traffic in Hormuz is disrupted. ‘Tipping point’ The escalation came after Trump said he would hold off on a major operation as Tehran was now getting “serious” in talks with Washington. “No I haven’t,” Trump told journalists in the Oval Office when asked if he had made a decision on hitting Iran hard, for now dialing back reports that he was increasingly frustrated with the war and mulling a large-scale military operation. “Look, we’re talking to them right now. I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.” Trump said Iran had a choice between making a deal or facing a “much higher level” of strikes, after nearly two weeks of US attacks that have left a ceasefire in tatters. The war that Trump once predicted would last four or five weeks is now nearing its fifth month, and is weighing on the Republican’s approval ratings ahead of crucial US midterm elections in November. Trump added that he did not know what the “tipping point” would be for a decision, but reiterated that his red line would be if Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon. The United States says it is carrying out the strikes to stop Iran closing the crucial Strait of Hormuz. Iran has responded with strikes on US bases that have killed four service members. The Iranian military said on Friday it had carried out attacks targeting US military assets in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, meanwhile, said they had targeted an Amazon data center in Bahrain, according to state media, though neither the US tech giant nor Bahrain has commented on the claim. There was also no confirmation from the United States of any targeting of its facilities or personnel. In Bahrain, sirens sounded again early on Saturday, the interior ministry said, urging residents to take shelter.

US announces visa restriction policy on cyber criminals, their immediate family members. WASHINGTON: The US has announced a new global visa restriction policy trageting foreign nationals involved in cybercrime and ​cyber-enabled crimes. Under the new policy, individuals engaged in online investment scams, sextortion and related offences — and their immediate family members — could be barred from entering the country. Announcing the policy, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the move was part of the Trump administration’s broader campaign to combat cybercrime, fraud and predatory online schemes targeting American citizens. Rubia said in a statement that Trump had made clear in an executive order that “his administration is taking action to counter an unprecedented threat from online investment scams”. The secretary said online investment scams, many allegedly “orchestrated by Chinese transnational criminal organisations, defrauded US citizens of at least $10 billion in 2024 while also fueling corruption, money laundering and human trafficking”. He added that American children had also been specifically targeted by overseas-based sextortion schemes, causing severe emotional and financial harm to victims and their families. Under the new policy, visa restrictions may be imposed on individuals found responsible for or complicit in cybercrime and cyber-enabled criminal activities, including cyberscams and sextortion, Rubio said, adding immediate family members of such individuals may also be subject to the restrictions. The statement added the US would use a range of measures — including, sanctions, criminal prosecutions, asset seizures, extradition requests and enhanced international law enforcement cooperation — to dismantle criminal networks operating across borders. “By restricting visa issuance to those who are responsible for or complicit in these criminal enterprises, we are sending a clear message: the United States will go after those who prey on our citizens,” Rubio said. Although the policy does not name any specific country other than referring to Chinese criminal organisations allegedly involved in investment scams, it applies globally and could affect nationals of any country found to be participating in cyber-enabled criminal activities.

Can Kabul hold?. The deceptive veneer of a monolithic and unyielding Taliban regime is rapidly giving way to profound structural decay, demonstrating that authoritarian societal suppression should not be conflated with institutional permanence or state capacity. Nearly five years after the fall of Kabul, the Taliban administration has reached a strategic impasse, balancing precariously on the precipice of a localised, multi-factional civil conflict. This impending instability is not merely a function of diplomatic isolation or international sanctions. Instead, it is being accelerated by an unsustainable internal economy of power, a volatile relationship with regional neighbours, and the emergence of decentralised, non-state resistance movements. Fissures within Domestically, the regime is fracturing along factional lines as the illusion of a unified command is replaced by a zero-sum power struggle between two competing power centres. On one side stands the radical Kandahar faction, a hyper-conservative clerical elite gathered around Supreme Leader Hibatullah Akhundzada, which clashes directly with the militarised Kabul faction led by figures like Sirajuddin Haqqani, who oversee day-to-day governance. Kandahar’s insistence on absolute ideological conformity and the centralisation of fiscal allocations has deeply alienated the field commanders responsible for winning the insurgency, privatising and paralysing the state’s administrative capacity while reducing the economy to a state of artificial survival dependent on illicit trade and irregular humanitarian inflows. This growing internal pressure is further compounded by a consolidating political opposition that directly rejects the Taliban’s claims of absolute control and popular legitimacy. Ahmad Massoud, the leader of the National Resistance Front (NRF), has challenged the regime’s narrative, explicitly dismissing the claim that anti-Taliban forces are fragmented or disconnected from the Afghan masses. Massoud posits that the fundamental path toward resolving the Afghan crisis reduces to a singular, foundational principle: returning the executive right to make decisions directly to the Afghan people. In his assessment, true national unity cannot be built upon a foundation of silence, fear, or the forced structural conformity imposed by the Taliban. Instead, a durable state architecture requires a system grounded in justice, mutual respect, and an institutional acceptance of Afghanistan’s diverse ethnic and cultural tapestry. Hence, the Taliban’s internal security architecture is increasingly challenged by a dual-layered opposition consisting of distinct factions deploying radically divergent operational strategies. While Ahmad Massoud’s NRF represents the formal, institutional wing of the resistance, drawing its lineage from the old political guard and maintaining a conventional military footprint in the northern valleys of Panjshir, Takhar, and Badakhshan, groups like Pasiban-i-Watan (Guardians of the Homeland) and the newer Sepahian-i-Mihan (Soldiers of the Homeland) operate as decentralised, grassroots phenomena. This forces the Taliban to simultaneously defend geographic frontiers in the north against the NRF and combat asymmetric sabotage from decentralised networks, overextending the regime’s security apparatus. A foreign policy blunder On the regional front, the failure of the Taliban’s foreign policy manifests in the collapse of its relationship with Pakistan, which further exposes its internal weaknesses. For decades, Islamabad served as a vital geopolitical corridor for Kabul, yet upon assuming power, the Taliban prioritised ideological solidarity with transnational militant networks over the strategic necessities of state-to-state bilateralism. By providing operational sanctuary, material support, and intelligence access to the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) terror outfit , the regime has enabled the group to execute lethal cross-border offensives, including incursions into regions like Chitral and sustained attacks across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. Recognising that the Taliban regime cannot or will not honour its counterterrorism obligations under regional frameworks, Islamabad has dismantled its policy of strategic patience in favour of kinetic deterrence and direct coercion. Following escalations in cross-border militancy, Pakistan initiated military actions, including Operation Ghazab lil-Haq, deploying targeted cross-border airstrikes against militant infrastructure. In response, Taliban officials have weaponised nationalist sentiment by rejecting the legitimacy of the Durand Line frontier and dismantling border fencing. This territorial defiance has led to sustained ground skirmishes at vital trade links like the Torkham crossing, disrupting regional commerce. Concurrently, the Taliban have accelerated diplomatic and strategic engagement with New Delhi, compounding Islamabad’s concerns vis-à-vis a revived two-front security threat. Russia’s pragmatic approach Desperate for external legitimacy to mitigate its domestic vulnerabilities, Kabul has also leveraged its diplomatic engagement with Moscow as evidence of international integration. Russia’s steps toward formal diplomatic engagement, including the removal of the Taliban from its official list of banned terrorist organisations, have been framed by Kabul as a major foreign policy success. However, despite its technical-military cooperation agreement, Moscow’s approach is transactional, born of realpolitik rather than genuine diplomatic trust, viewing the Taliban as a buffer against the regional expansion of the Islamic State-Khorasan (IS-K) terror group. Within Kremlin, pragmatic engagement with Kabul coexists with deep skepticism over the Taliban’s long-term capability and strategic intent. Russian analyst Andrei Serenko, head of the Russian Centre for Contemporary Afghanistan Studies, has drawn attention to the internal vulnerabilities of the Taliban rule and the emergence of new resistance dynamics that could further complicate Afghanistan’s security landscape and ultimately regional peace and stability. Taliban’s continued ties with regional radical groups, including the TTP, which Russia also has designated as a terrorist organisation, heavily cloud Moscow’s strategic calculations. This is a central paradox confronting Russia’s Afghan policy: Moscow requires a sufficiently stable authority in Kabul to contain the IS-K, and facilitate its broader Eurasian ambitions, yet the durability of that authority is increasingly tested by internal factionalism, political resistance, decentralised terrorist networks, and deteriorating relations with Pakistan. Ultimately, the Taliban regime is trapped between a deeply aggrieved neighbour to the east, mounting domestic resistance from within, and cautious partners to the north. The current stability in Afghanistan may therefore prove more fragile than territorial control suggests. Unless it shifts away from ideological rigidity and addresses political, security, and regional contradictions accumulating beneath its rule, Afghanistan risks sliding once again toward fragmented sovereignty and conflict.

'Betrayal' after years of sacrifice: The young victims of India's exam leak scandal. Growing up with a chronically ill mother in a remote village in India, Rema Begum aspired to become a doctor until her dream was cut short by her own tragic death. After years of studying and costly coaching classes, the 20-year-old believed she had finally done enough to win a coveted seat at a government medical school. Then came news that the question paper of the medical entrance examination she sat for had been leaked, and a retest was ordered. Days later, Begum was dead. She was among at least 20 students who reportedly took their own lives after the incident, according to local media and activists. The exam paper leak, alongside a string of other irregularities, has fuelled nationwide protests and public anger over an education system many students say is stacked against them. A month after her death, Begum’s father Rajaul Islam is still struggling to understand how his “gem” of a daughter lost hope. But he believes the retest announcement changed everything. “After the exam, she was absolutely confident that she would clear it,” Islam told AFP by phone from the family’s village in the northeastern state of Assam. “But after a retest was announced because the paper had leaked, she became a different person and withdrew into a shell.” Nothing the family said could reassure her, he said. Islam, a fish trader, had spent heavily on his daughter’s preparation, sending her to coaching centres in larger cities for two years. “I had spent a lot of money on her studies, so she was worried it would all go to waste,” he said. ‘Happy life’ Days before the new exam date, Begum was found dead. Her death highlights the immense pressures on students in India, where admission to a government-run medical college remains one of the most sought after pathways to economic security. Despite rapid growth in the world’s most populous country, millions of young people still face a shortage of well-paying jobs and fierce competition for professional careers. “Getting through the NEET examination therefore means, for many families, the assurance of a happy and comfortable life,” said literary scholar and former professor G.N. Devy, referring to the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET). “But the number of students who want these places is completely out of proportion to the number of institutions available.” More than two million candidates sat the exam this year, competing for roughly 137,000 medical seats nationwide. The odds have fuelled a sprawling coaching industry where students spend years preparing, often at enormous sacrifice for their families. In Rajasthan, farmer Rajesh Kumar sold ancestral land and borrowed 1.1m rupees ($11,400) so his son Pradeep Meena could attend coaching classes for three years. “I toiled for up to 16 hours a day on the farm so that he could take coaching classes,” Kumar told AFP . “Because I thought if he becomes a doctor it would all be worth it, and I could lead a comfortable life in my old age.” After the exam, Meena appeared certain he had succeeded. Kumar recalled his son hugging him and saying that “even God cannot stop me from becoming a doctor now”. A day after authorities announced the retest, the 22-year-old died by suicide. ‘Betrayed’ In Uttar Pradesh, another family suffered a similar loss after the death of their 21-year-old son Ritik Mishra. “It was his third attempt, and he said he had done well this time,” said his father, Anup Kumar Mishra, referring to the exam. His son took his own life a day after news of the exam leak surfaced. For students who eventually retook the test, the experience was draining. “It is very demoralising mentally,” said 19-year-old Chaitanya Aggarwal. “You give your best and then you are forced to take it again.” Teachers say the emotional toll should not be underestimated. “It’s a highly stressful experience to prepare for and take the exam, and having to do it all over again is not easy,” said Abhijit Patra, a teacher at a coaching centre in the eastern city of Kolkata. “Paper leaks make an already hectic experience even worse.” For many families, the scandal felt like a “betrayal” after years of sacrifice, said Devy, the former professor. Preparing for entrance examinations was often financially ruinous and socially exhausting, he said, particularly for lower-income households unable to afford costly private universities or education abroad. “They begin this journey of preparation with hope, so when they discover the paper has leaked or been sold, they feel betrayed,” Devy said. Thousands of kilometres from the protest site in capital New Delhi, Begum’s family is still searching for answers. “I request the government to take irregularities in examinations seriously,” her father said. “They should understand that it is not easy for a child from a poor family to dream of a better life and work towards it.”

Controversial posts case: IHC rules Imaan, Hadi's sentence suspension pleas admissible. ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Saturday declared the petitions filed by human rights activist and lawyer Imaan Mazari and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha seeking the suspension of their sentences in the controversial tweets case as admissible. Justice Muhammad Azam Khan announced the verdict, that was reserved on Friday, and rejected the prosecution’s miscellaneous application seeking the dismissal of the petitions on grounds of premature filing. During the proceedings, the prosecution had maintained that the petitions filed by Imaan and Hadi were premature and therefore not maintainable at this stage. However, after hearing arguments from both sides, the IHC rejected the prosecution’s objection and declared the petitions admissible for hearing. The verdict now clears the way for the please seeking the suspension of the sentences to proceed for hearing. On January 24, rights lawyers Imaan and Hadi were sentenced by an Islamabad sessions court to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). Following their convictions, which were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts , the couple challenged their convictions before the IHC on February 7. The case stems from a complaint filed under Peca on Aug 12, 2025 by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency’s (NCCIA) Islamabad assistant director (investigating officer). The NCCIA complaint accused Imaan of disseminating and “propagating narratives that align with hostile terrorist groups and proscribed organisations”, while her husband was implicated for reposting some of her posts. The FIR of the case alleged that the two held security forces responsible for cases of missing persons in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. It also stated that they had portrayed the armed forces as ineffective against proscribed groups, including the banned outfits Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

Mustafa Kamal rails against injustice meted out to Karachi, says MQM-P will now take to the streets. Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) leader Mustafa Kamal on Saturday announced that the party would take to the streets against the injustice being meted out to Karachi. Kamal, who is also the federal health minister, made the announcement while addressing a press conference in Karachi, where he railed against the Sindh government’s indifference towards the metropolis and its people. “MQM-P has decided that it will no longer stay quiet. We will adopt all the ways listed in the Constitution. We spoke in assemblies, they do not agree. We presented a constitutional amendment, they do not agree. Now, we will make use of the streets while staying within the law and the Constitution. We will come onto the streets with the people,” he said. “The law and the Constitution give us the right to come out onto the streets. Pakistan is at a point where it cannot function under the same system any longer,” he said. This system, he said, was the one with four provinces and a federating unit. Referring to the distribution of federal funds, Kamal said the federation had allocated Rs8.4 trillion among the four provinces, of which Sindh received around Rs2.2 trillion. “These funds are allocated in the name of the people, but they remain confined to the Chief Minister House instead of reaching Karachi, Larkana, Hyderabad or Sukkur,” he alleged. He said that funds dispensed to Sindh were never seen by the districts, adding that there was no system for disbursing the funds to union councils. “And they say they will not touch the 18th Amendment. The 18th Amendment has not been enforced. That is why MQM-P announces that it will endorse all steps for the devolution of power … the top of the list of which is new provinces on an administrative basis,” he said. During the presser, Kamal accused the Sindh government of preventing Karachi from playing its role in driving Pakistan’s economic growth, alleging that the provincial administration had failed to provide the city with basic civic services. He also questioned why Karachi was being held back despite its economic importance. “Who can pull Pakistan out of this economic quagmire? And who is preventing Karachi from playing that role? It is the current Sindh government that is not allowing Karachi to contribute to Pakistan as it should,” he said. Kamal said the provincial government was holding Karachi back and preventing it from contributing to the country’s development. “We are happy for Lahore, but the tragedy is that if development was to take place anywhere in Pakistan first, it should have happened in Karachi,” he said. The minister said Karachi should have led Pakistan’s progress and helped the country emerge from its economic challenges, but alleged that the PPP-led Sindh government had failed to allow the city to fulfil that role. He also accused the provincial administration of failing to provide residents with basic services, alleging that Karachi lacked adequate drinking water, a proper sewerage system and sufficient schools, while many girls’ schools did not even have toilets. He further alleged that the province had the country’s highest rates of child stunting and out of school children. He said that Sindh also reported more dog-bite cases than any other province, adding that incidents of children falling into open manholes were a recurring problem in Karachi. “Sindh is the only place where children are losing their lives after falling into manholes,” he said. Calling Karachi Pakistan’s “economic capital”, Kamal said the city generated revenue for the country and housed its seaports, yet continued to suffer from poor governance. “It is an international city, yet news of children falling into manholes emerges from Karachi. Lawlessness is at its peak, there is no one to look after primary and secondary schools, and there have been no police reforms,” he said. The minister contrasted Karachi’s condition with developments in other parts of the country, saying that while other cities were discussing air ambulances, metro systems and trains, Karachi was introducing bicycle ambulances. “I want to tell those running the country not to mistake our silence for weakness. Hyderabad, Karachi, Sukkur and other cities are home to living, breathing people, but everywhere there is destruction,” he said. Kamal said the MQM-P had proposed constitutional amendments aimed at addressing these issues, but they could not be passed because the party lacked the required numbers in parliament. “Will our generations continue to suffer because this government needs the PPP’s numbers? From Karachi to Kashmore, our children are dying while political and democratic oppression continues,” he alleged.

AJK Election Commission warns against violating code after PML-N’s pre-poll promises. MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission on Saturday warned that it would not allow any individual or institution to violate the code of conduct, amid a controversy over development pledges made by the PML-N during the ongoing election campaign. The warning came after former prime minister Nawaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz announced development schemes, including the ‘gift’ of 10 e-buses at election rallies in Muzaffarabad and Mirpur. The announcement did not go over well with the PPP, which described it as “political bribery”. It subsequently approached the Election Commission, urging it to take notice of what it termed a violation of the election code of conduct. An Election Commission spokesperson said federal and provincial ministers were free to participate in electioneering in AJK but could not use official protocol, government resources or the state machinery for electoral purposes. The spokesperson warned that the announcement of any new development scheme, financial package, public facility or welfare project during the election campaign would amount to a violation of the code of conduct. Any vehicles, equipment, relief goods or other facilities sent by the federal or provincial governments during the election period would be confiscated and action taken in accordance with the law, the statement added. The spokesperson urged all ministers, candidates and political parties to strictly observe the code of conduct to ensure free, fair and transparent elections and maintain public confidence in the electoral process. Meanwhile, AJK Secretary Information Muhammad Rashid Hanif and Director Information Tariq Jamil Durrani urged journalists and media organisations to ensure responsible, impartial and professional coverage of the elections. In a joint message, they called on the media to publish only verified and balanced information, avoid rumours and inflammatory content, and adhere to the Election Commission’s code of conduct and journalistic ethics. They also urged users of social media platforms to refrain from sharing unverified or misleading material that could undermine the electoral process or disturb public order.

Italian embassy, teen apologise after confrontation with Thai woman on Bangkok train. A viral video of a Thai woman confronting a group of noisy Italian teenagers who exchange vulgar words and gestures on a Bangkok train prompted online backlash and an apology from Italy’s embassy on Saturday. The TikTok video, posted on Friday, was shared more than 28,000 times with the caption: “What nationality are they?? Is it time for Thailand to stop free visas yet?” In the clip, a Thai woman off-camera is heard repeatedly telling the Italian group to be quiet. “In Thailand, we don’t scream,” she says, before a woman from the group replies: “Sorry for bringing money to your country.” One boy was filmed waving and then gesturing to the camera with only his middle finger raised. The dispute escalated as the Thai woman accused the Italians of having “no manners” — and then also used vulgar language and gestures. The incident has divided opinion online, with some internet users criticising the teenagers for impropriety and disrespecting local customs, while others said the Thai woman reacted too harshly. The Italian Embassy in Bangkok said it condemned the “inappropriate behaviour of a group of Italian underage tourists” on a school trip and apologised “to the people of Thailand and to everyone affected”. “Italians deeply understand and appreciate the values that Thai society places on respect for others, courtesy, and harmonious coexistence,” the embassy said in a statement posted on Facebook. The embassy also shared a video featuring three adults, who identified themselves as “leaders” of the Italian group, and the boy filmed raising his middle finger, with each apologising to Thai people. One woman said the teen would be “returning to Italy as soon as possible” on account of his behaviour. The TikTok user who posted the video did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment. Thailand cut the length of visa-free stays for tourists in May as part of efforts to curb crimes committed by foreign nationals. The move followed a series of high-profile arrests of foreigners over drug offences, sex trafficking, public indecency and operating unlicensed businesses. Thailand’s economy relies heavily on tourism, but foreign arrivals have yet to return to pre-Covid-19 levels. Total tourist arrivals dropped more than three per cent in the first half of this year compared to the same period in 2025, with visitors from Italy down around 9.6pc, according to the latest tourism ministry figures.

3 more terrorists killed in Mastung IBO, taking tally to 13. Security forces have killed three more terrorists in an ongoing intelligence-based operation (IBO) in the Khad Kocha area of Balochistan’s Mastung district, state-run Radio Pakistan reported on Saturday, citing security sources. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, in a statement commending the security forces, also confirmed the development. The security operation , conducted under an indefinite curfew , was launched after a shooting on a Karachi-bound coach coming from Quetta claimed three lives and injured five others on Wednesday. On Saturday, Radio Pakistan quoted security sources as saying that “Fitna al-Hindustan has suffered further losses” in the IBO, which has been dubbed Operation Al-Azm. The government uses the term “ Fitna al-Hindustan ” for Balochistan-based groups to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. “The number of terrorists killed so far during Operation Al-Azm has reached 13,” Radio Pakistan reported. Six of these had been killed on Thursday and another four were eliminated a day ago. Security sources said that several hideouts “belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan ” were destroyed. They added that weapons, ammunition and materials used for making improvised explosive devices (IEDs) were also recovered. “There are also confirmed reports that several terrorists belonging to Fitna ul Hindustan were injured during the operation,” Radio Pakistan stated. In his statement, Naqvi commended the professionalism of security forces in their counterterrorism efforts, state-run APP reported. Noting that security forces were conducting effective operations against terrorists across Balochistan as part of Operation Al-Azm, he specifically lauded the actions in Khad Kocha. The interior minister stated that 13 terrorists have been “killed in operations conducted under Operation Al-Azm so far”. Naqvi said operations by security forces would continue until terrorism was eliminated from Balochistan. On Thursday , besides six terrorists being killed, officials also claimed the arrest of female suicide bombers and several other suspects who were considered to be working as facilitators for the attackers. The same day, District and Sessions Judge Abdul Hakeem Kakar and his guard were gunned down , and another judge was among two injured when they came under attack by armed men while heading to Mastung. The gun attack followed security forces killing three terrorists in Mastung, where the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said two suicide bombers and their facilitator were also apprehended. Another seven terrorists were eliminated in Surab district. Amid the clearance operation in Mastung, the provincial leadership on Friday emphasised the need for a political resolution to the ongoing crisis. Speaking to political and tribal leaders, Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langove reiterated the government’s commitment to dialogue and said the parliament remained the most effective platform for political parties to present their views, concerns and demands. Security concerns have heightened in Balochistan after a spate of major terrorist attacks took place earlier this month, which prompted counterterrorism operations across the province. Among the counterterrorism efforts was Operation Shaban , in which 91 terrorists were killed between July 5 and July 16, according to security sources cited by state media. This took the tally of terrorists eliminated in operations across the province during the period to 129.

'Cockroaches won': India's education minister resigns after days of youth protests. India’s Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan said on Saturday he has resigned from his position, handing a major victory to youth protesters nationwide who demanded that he quit to take responsibility for examination paper leaks . India’s biggest street protests of recent years had become a political flashpoint, posing one of the biggest challenges to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi as opposition politicians joined youngsters’ calls to demand action and disrupted parliament. The minister announced his resignation on X just as police fired tear gas to scatter young protesters in Delhi, hours before their leaders were set to hold another round of talks with ministers to push for the move. In a two-page statement shared on X, Pradhan said he has sent his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. “Considering the situation that has developed at Jantar Mantar and across the country — that anti-national forces should not take advantage of this situation, that the unity of the country should be preserved, that not even a single Indian student’s future should get entangled in legal complications, and that our children should devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers — I have sent my resignation to the honourable prime minister,” The Times of India quoted the letter as stating. The self-named Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) youth movement, which has been at the helm of the protests, welcomed the resignation by stating on its X account, “Cockroaches won.. Democracy won!” “We have done it,” said CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke to loud cheers at the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi. However, he added, “We have two more demands. We won’t go like this.” Dipke demanded that the families of all students who reportedly took their own lives after the exam leak should receive 10 million Indian rupees in compensation. “This [resignation] is for them,” he said , pointing towards a banner with the pictures of 20 students whom activists say died following the exam leak. Secondly, he demanded that action be taken against police officials involved in the July 20 crackdown on protesters. “Remember, do not mess with cockroach,” he cautioned. Dipke also called for all cases registered against students to be withdrawn. “We are cockroaches. Once it enters, it does not leave,” he quipped. Another post by CJP listed three demands as “pending”, with the third being a public apology from the Rapid Action Force (RAF) and Delhi Police. Dipke also urged his supporters not to turn him into a “hero” because of Pradhan’s resignation. “Do not make this mistake. Do not make me a hero because of Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation. The country has been ruined because of making one person a hero.” He further said , “When we rise above Hindu and Muslim politics and talk about issues, then it will be good for the country.” Supporters of the “cockroach” movement had been protesting since June , but anger boiled over since police on Monday injured dozens of students, launching baton charges and firing tear gas to deter crowds of protesters marching on parliament. Youth celebrates Protesters continuing their sit-in at Jantar Mantar, the same site of Monday’s police crackdown, erupted in joy after Pradhan’s announcement. They shouted “Jai Hind”, a patriotic slogan meaning “Victory to India”, as the national anthem played on loudspeakers and sweets were distributed among the crowd. At least 1,000 police officials stood nearby guarding the area, according to Reuters journalists at the site. View this post on Instagram The protests also reflected anger over job scarcity, corruption and government accountability. “Young generation is here. This is a win for the constitution, protester Tluanga Ralte said, walking with a copy of the Indian constitution at the protest site after the minister’s resignation. “We are not a lazy generation.” Federal authorities even on Saturday restricted access to the internet and to 18 metro stations to try to limit the protest in the capital, the latest day of such restrictions. Students, youth activists and opposition supporters had in recent days staged protests in the states of West Bengal, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, holding placards demanding Pradhan’s resignation and boycotting classes in some places. ‘Not a matter of personal reputation’ Pradhan, 57, is a senior leader of Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and has been regarded as a rising figure, and even mentioned in the past as a potential BJP leader. “From day one, I took responsibility for this and never turned away from this situation,” the education minister asserted in his letter today, referring to the exam leaks. Pradhan said the government took immediate notice when irregularities emerged in the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET-UG) held on May 3. “The Government of India took immediate cognisance of this, handed over the investigation to the CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation), cancelled the exam, and announced a new date for re-examination. Alongside this, it was also decided to conduct the exam in CBT (Computer-Based Test) mode from next year,” he highlighted. In his letter, the minister also accused “certain individuals occupying positions of responsibility” of trying to mislead students and create obstacles. Pradhan stated: “I have always been an unwavering believer in the strength of our democracy and I have always held deep respect for the aspirations, dreams and expectations of the youth. They are not only the future of India, but also the bearers, builders, and architects of a new and developed India. “Watching the events of the last 10 days has saddened me. This is not a matter of personal reputation for me.” Pradhan concluded his letter saying, “My resolve is that we will not let the country’s youth get caught in a web of confusion.” A minister since Modi first took office in 2014, he has held the petroleum and natural gas, steel, skill development and education portfolios, becoming education minister in 2021. His father was a veteran BJP leader and served as a junior federal minister between 1998 and 2004. ‘Victory of democracy’ Supporters of CJP, including the opposition Congress party, welcomed Pradhan’s resignation. FIA sets up investigation unit to trace criminals operating on the dark web. ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has set up a dedicated dark web investigation unit to track and prosecute criminals operating in the shadowy realm, to effectively counter threats to the country’s interests emanating from encrypted online platforms, officials said on Saturday. Housed in the state-of-the-art National Command and Control Centre (NC3) at FIA headquarters, the unit will use modern technology to overcome obfuscation techniques employed by criminals to identify them, track dubious transactions usually carried out through cryptocurrency, and execute enforcement actions, FIA Director General Dr Usman Anwar told Dawn . He said the unit will focus on tracing criminal networks involved in creating illegal documents that facilitate human trafficking and illegal migrant smuggling and other similar subjects within the ambit of the FIA. The dark web refers to websites that are not indexed by search engi­nes, and are usually encry­pted, only accessible through specialised browsers. It can be an effective cloak for criminals because it leverages cutting-edge technologies to hide their identity. Criminals take advantage of its decentralisation and anonymity to indulge in numerous illegal activities, including hiring a hitman for assassination, trading drugs and weapons, selling stolen classified data and credentials, terrorism, piracy, malware, and hacking tools. There is no clear path for conducting investigations and enforcement action on businesses that operate on the dark web. These businesses are not only decentralised, but the criminal activities they facilitate tend to be transnational. The only way for authorities to respond is to fight technology with technology and forge greater international cooperation. DG Anwar said that working hand in hand with the cryptocurrency investigation unit under the same roof, the dark web investigation unit would use its blockchain forensic capability to connect pseudonymous addresses to real-world identities using open-source intelligence (Osint) as an additional tool for better investigative outcomes with documentary evidence. “We will leverage advanced tools and methodologies to meticulously investigate individuals on the dark web, cross-referencing aliases, usernames, and pseudonyms across marketplaces, forums and sites,” the FIA DG said. He added that the investigative process would help build detailed profiles of criminal actors, enabling authorities to bring them to justice. FIA’s NC3 Director Dr Athar Waheed explained that the internet was often described in three layers: the surface web, the deep web, and the dark web. These layers differ in visibility, accessibility and intended use. The surface web consists of publicly accessible websites indexed by standard search engines like Google. It includes news sites, blogs, online stores, and social media platforms. Anyone with a browser and internet connection can access these pages without special tools or permissions. The deep web refers to all web content that is not indexed by search engines. This includes databases, academic journals behind paywalls, webmail accounts, online banking, and intranet systems. Although not visible to search engines, these resources are typically legitimate and require credentials, subscriptions, or specific queries to access. The dark web is a subset of the deep web that is intentionally hidden and accessible only through specialised anonymity-preserving software, such as Tor (The Onion Router). The NC3 director explained that Tor was an open-source overlay network built on free and open-source software run by over 7,000 volunteer-operated relays worldwide, as well as by millions of users who route their internet traffic via random paths through these relays, enabling anonymous communication. Unlike the deep web, which primarily consists of private but conventional web content, the dark web includes hidden services that use encryption and obscure IP addresses to protect identities. Accessing it requires knowledge of its specific tools and protocols.

Trump bashes 'fake news,' stokes 2028 furore in press gala rerun. US President Donald Trump lashed out at “fake news media” and talked about serving a banned third term as he addressed a rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Dinner on Friday, three months after an assassination attempt disrupted the event. “This place is really the largest group of Trump derangement syndrome people ever put together at one time,” Trump told the media gala at the Waldorf Astoria hotel in Washington, DC. The 80-year-old started with a relatively conciliatory tone, reflecting on the attack by a gunman that forced him to be evacuated from the dinner in April. “The show must go on,” Trump said. But he quickly pivoted to attacking a wide range of perceived enemies in an often rambling speech, starting with journalists before training his fire on Democratic opponents. Trump had earlier thrown up his hands and laughed as he shook hands with a Wall Street Journal team that broke stories on his ties to disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein. But he later joked that “this has not been an easy evening, all these awards,” Trump said after journalists received prizes for their reporting on the Republican’s second presidency. Trump also revived talk about serving a third term, which is barred under the US Constitution, even as he insisted he was joking. “Just like my presidency, the second time is always better. And the third time is better yet,” Trump said, before adding: “I’m only kidding.” He later doubled down, pulling out a red “Trump 2028” cap and saying he was “pleased to announce my intention to — and this is a somewhat of a scoop — my intention to run for a fourth term as president of the United States.” Much of Trump’s speech seemed to recycle his campaign-style rallies, with the president even jokingly lambasting his speechwriters when some lines fell flat. But he ended the hour-long speech by saying he had “tremendous respect” for the journalists in the room — while adding: “When I’m gone you’re all going to be broke.” Bad blood Trump, who was attending his first White House Correspondents Dinner after years of bad blood with the press, added that he planned to come next year too. He returned amid heightened security on Friday, three months after an alleged assassination attempt forced his chaotic evacuation from the event after gunshots were fired at the Washington Hilton and the black-tie dinner was called off. California man Cole Allen, 31, has pleaded not guilty to charges including attempting to kill the president. US President Donald Trump speaks during the 2026 White House Correspondents’ Association (WHCA) Dinner at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, DC, the USA on July 24, 2026. — AFP This time the US Secret Service took no chances. Police and National Guard officers sealed off nearby roads and threw up a major security cordon, although guests passing through faced only a cursory check. The venue was changed from the Hilton to the Waldorf Astoria, a former Trump hotel, meaning the gala will be much smaller and “more intimate,” according to organisers. “Let’s try this again,” said CBS correspondent Weijia Jiang, the outgoing president of the White House Correspondents’ Association, who presided over the previous dinner. “Tonight our message is this: We are back. We will not be intimidated. We will not let an act of violence have the final word.” Incoming WHCA president Jacqui Heinrich said the event would return to the Washington Hilton next year. ‘Threat picture’ US Secret Service Director Sean Curran was spotted standing in the entrance hall watching guests arrive, an AFP reporter saw. Guests waited in a long line to show a QR code and their ID on the way into the atrium where the dinner was held. Along with Trump’s speech, the rescheduled dinner included a performance by mentalist Oz Pearlman and a tribute to a Secret Service agent who helped stop the alleged gunman in April. Israeli-US magician Oz “Oz the Mentalist” Pearlman performs during the 2026 White House Correspondents’ Association (WHCA) Dinner at the Waldorf Astoria in Washington, DC, the US on July 24, 2026. — AFP Curran, the head of the Secret Service, defended security at the original event, telling reporters “it did work, the system worked.” He insisted a cordon had prevented the alleged attacker from reaching the main hall in April. But Curran, who was at Trump’s side when an assassin’s bullet hit the Republican’s ear at an election rally in 2024, said that current threats against top US officials were “off the charts”. “The threat picture and environment is as large as I’ve ever seen it,” added Curran.

Valenzuela gov’t supports Baby Ayla’s liver transplant in India. Baby Ayla, a Valenzuela City resident diagnosed with biliary atresia -- a rare and life threatening liver condition -- will undergo a transplant in India with support from the local government. The city’s Public Information Office said doctors recommended urgent surgery. While officials initially prepared assistance through a foundation partner at Chinese General Hospital, Ayla’s family chose to pursue treatment abroad. To back that decision, the city extended financial aid to cover airfare and hotel accommodations during the operation and recovery. This latest support follows earlier interventions. In October 2025, the family received medical assistance, and in March 2026, the City Social Welfare and Development Office continued case management and monitoring. Officials stressed that Valenzuela remains committed to standing with Baby Ayla and her family as they hope for a successful surgery and recovery.

Coca-Cola supports stronger PET bottle recovery across Metro Manila. As urban communities face growing waste management challenges, collection infrastructure plays a more critical role in keeping recyclable materials within the recycling loop. Across Metro Manila, Coca-Cola Europacific Aboitiz Philippines (CCEAP), the bottling arm and official distributor of Coca-Cola products in the country, has been supporting local government units (LGUs) and community partners in strengthening PET bottle recovery and waste diversion efforts through infrastructure support and long-term collaboration. Through partnerships with the cities of Manila, Pasig, Valenzuela, Quezon City, and Caloocan, CCEAP has provided baling machines and collection bins to help improve PET bottle recovery at the local level. Baling machines compress collected PET bottles into compact bales, reducing storage requirements and improving transport efficiency. This enables partner communities to recover and move more recyclable materials, helping divert valuable resources away from landfills and the environment. These initiatives contribute to CCEAP’s broader commitment to supporting community-based recycling systems and advancing PET bottle circularity in the Philippines. “Effective recovery and recycling systems are built through collaboration. By working with local governments and community partners, we can make PET bottle collection more efficient and accessible where it matters most. These partnerships help ensure that more plastic packaging is collected, recovered, and returned to the recycling value chain,” says Atty. Juan Lorenzo Tañada, VP for Corporate & Regulatory Affairs of Coca-Cola Europacific Aboitiz Philippines (CCEAP). The City Government of Manila was among the first LGUs in the region to establish a sustainability-focused partnership with CCEAP. Since then, the collaboration has helped strengthen waste management and diversion efforts at the city's Materials Recovery Facility (MRF), enabling the more efficient processing and recovery of PET bottles, single-use plastics, aluminum cans, and other recyclable materials. “The baling machine has significantly improved our operations and our logistics. PET bottles that were previously stored loose can now be processed into compact bales, allowing us to transport more recyclables on fewer trips,” shares Engr. John Vaughn Caoyong, Public Service Assistant at the city’s Department of Environment and Public Services (DEPS). “Collection bins have also been deployed in high-traffic areas across the city, such as the Manila Zoological and Botanical Garden and Manila City Hall. The Tapon to Ipon program, in partnership with Coca-Cola, has enabled the city to strengthen its participation in an efficient recycling ecosystem,” adds Engr. Caoyong. Successful partnerships are built on a shared commitment to meaningful change. In Pasig City, this comes to life through the Innovation for Circular Economy (ICE) Hub, which advances circular economy practices while supporting local communities and MSMEs. This aligns with CCEAP's Tapon to Ipon program, which engages sari-sari stores as collection hubs and partners in resource recovery. “Coca-Cola was among the first to donate a baling machine to support our facility operations. The baling machine has helped improve the way we handle PET bottles and other recyclables, allowing us to process materials more efficiently. We’re able to maximize the hub's operations in building a more circular and sustainable waste management system for our community,” says EnP. Allendri Angeles, MMEP Head, Pasig City Solid Waste Management Office and ICE Hub. CCEAP has also partnered with the City Government of Valenzuela to boost local PET bottle recovery and enable more scalable recycling solutions. The company recently turned over a baling machine to the Barangay Ugong MRF. “Environmental stewardship is a shared responsibility. This partnership demonstrates how the public and private sectors can work together to strengthen waste management systems, support our environmental goals, and encourage communities to take an active role in creating a lasting positive impact. Through collective action, we can build a more sustainable and resilient Valenzuela City,” says Rachel Torres, Valenzuela CENRO Officer-in-Charge. In Quezon City, the turnover of a baling machine has enabled collectors from Palerong Manggagawa ng Payatas to scale up their operations with an improved capacity to collect, process, and divert more recyclable materials to recovery partners. “The baling equipment has helped us increase the volume of recyclables we can process and deliver. Before, we collected around 600 kilos every two weeks. Today, we can deliver as much as one to two tons in a week, with the bottles taking up less space and becoming easier to transport. It has helped us become more efficient and expand our recovery efforts across Quezon City,” says Mark Angelo Jacob, President of Palerong Manggagawa ng Payatas. CCEAP has also provided two baling machines to the Caloocan City MRF as part of another partnership aimed at boosting waste management infrastructure and improving recovery processes. These partnerships are part of the Coca-Cola system's Tapon to Ipon initiative, a nationwide PET bottle collection program that works with communities, local governments, government agencies, micro-retailers, and other partners to make PET bottle recovery and recycling more accessible. Since its launch in 2021, the program has expanded collection networks across the country through collection hubs, awareness campaigns, and infrastructure support. Beyond Metro Manila, CCEAP has partnered with local governments across the Philippines to help institutionalize accessible and efficient collection systems and recycling infrastructure. Key partners include the Island Garden City of Samal; the municipalities of Baganga in Davao Oriental, Malay in Aklan, San Juan in Batangas, Del Carmen and General Luna in Surigao del Norte; the cities of Koronadal, Baguio, Dumaguete, and Naga, in partnership with the CamSur Multipurpose Cooperative; the provinces of Iloilo and Palawan; and the Province of Quirino through the Union of Local Authorities of the Philippines (ULAP). The goal is to keep PET bottles within the value chain and to be recycled again. For some of these communities, the collected PET bottles are diverted to PETValue Philippines, the country's pioneering food-grade, bottle-to-bottle recycling facility. A joint venture between CCEAP and global sustainable chemicals company Indorama Ventures, PETValue transforms post-consumer PET plastic bottles into food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) that can be made into new beverage bottles, advancing PET circularity in the country. As more communities take part in collection and recovery efforts, partnerships among local governments, community organizations, and industry stakeholders continue to demonstrate the power of collective action in creating cleaner and more sustainable communities for future generations.

The 1975's Matty Healy marries Gabbriette Bechtel. The 1975 frontman Matty Healy has married model and musician Gabbriette Bechtel in an intimate ceremony held on July 18 at Castillo del Lago in Los Angeles, according to multiple international reports. Photos and videos from the wedding quickly spread online, showing the couple sharing a kiss at the altar. Healy wore a classic black tuxedo, while Gabbriette walked down the aisle in a white bridal gown with a traditional veil and half-up hairstyle. Representatives for the couple confirmed the marriage to People, saying the ceremony was attended by family and close friends. Guests reportedly included Charli XCX and her husband George Daniel—Healy's bandmate in The 1975—as well as Anastasia Karanikolaou, Fai Khadra, Alex Consani, Devon Lee Carlson and fiancé Duke Nicholson, Sydney Lynn Carlson, Tyrell Hampton, Alex O'Connor, and Quenlin Blackwell. Healy and Swift were briefly linked in 2024, with fans speculating that their relationship inspired "The Smallest Man Who Ever Lived" from The Tortured Poets Department, though Swift has never confirmed the song's inspiration.

Jo Koy, Nicole Scherzinger join Hollywood Walk of Fame as Lea Salonga's historic ceremony draws near. The excitement surrounding Lea Salonga's upcoming Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony just got even bigger. Weeks after it was confirmed that the Broadway legend will become the first full-blooded Filipina to receive a star on the famed Hollywood Boulevard on Sept. 4, two more entertainers with Filipino roots, comedian Jo Koy and singer-actress Nicole Scherzinger, have been named to the Hollywood Walk of Fame Class of 2027. Within a little over a year, three entertainers of Filipino descent have been selected for one of entertainment's most recognizable public honors. Taken together, the announcements mark one of the strongest periods of Filipino representation in the landmark's history. The Hollywood Chamber of Commerce announced the 32-member Class of 2027 on Thursday during a news conference at Funko Hollywood on Hollywood Boulevard. "The Walk of Fame Selection Committee is proud to welcome the Class of 2027 to one of the most enduring symbols of achievement in entertainment," committee chairman Peter Roth said. "These extraordinary individuals have each made a lasting impact on audiences around the world through their talent, creativity and dedication to their craft." Jo Koy and Scherzinger will both be honored in the Live Theatre/Live Performance category alongside acclaimed Italian ballet dancer Roberto Bolle. Their selection continues the growing presence of Filipino names on one of Hollywood's most famous sidewalks. Before Salonga's selection in 2025, the Walk of Fame had already honored Bruno Mars, Black Eyed Peas member apl.de.ap and actor Rob Schneider, each reflecting the increasing impact of artists with Filipino heritage on the global entertainment industry. For Filipinos, every new addition carries significance beyond individual achievement. Each star serves as a permanent reminder of the growing influence of Filipino artists on the world stage, especially in an industry where Asian representation has historically been limited. Established in 1960, the Hollywood Walk of Fame remains one of the entertainment industry's most enduring symbols of success. More than 2,800 terrazzo-and-brass stars now line Hollywood Boulevard and Vine Street, recognizing outstanding contributions to motion pictures, television, recording, radio, live theatre/live performance and sports entertainment. Unlike traditional awards, a Walk of Fame star is earned through a nomination and selection process. Nominations may be submitted by fans, organizations, studios, record labels and other representatives before being reviewed by the Walk of Fame Selection Committee. Honorees must have at least five years of professional achievement in their field, demonstrate charitable or community involvement, and commit to attending their unveiling ceremony. Scherzinger first rose to international fame as the lead singer of the Pussycat Dolls before establishing herself as a solo artist, television personality and acclaimed stage performer. Her recent work in "Sunset Boulevard" has earned widespread critical praise. Jo Koy, meanwhile, has become one of the world's top stand-up comedians by turning stories about his Filipino family, particularly his mother, into relatable routines that have introduced Filipino culture to audiences around the globe. The Class of 2027 also includes Pedro Pascal, Lisa Kudrow, Idris Elba, Kate Hudson, Adam Scott, Karol G, Sia, Linkin Park, Lil Wayne and former NFL coach Jimmy Johnson. As for Salonga, her Sept. 4 ceremony is shaping up to be another milestone not only for her celebrated career but also for Filipino representation in Hollywood. Best known for originating the role of Kim in "Miss Saigon," winning a Tony Award, and providing the singing voices of Disney princesses Jasmine and Mulan, Salonga has long been regarded as one of the Philippines' most accomplished performers on the world stage. Her unveiling will coincide with the 2026 Manila International Film Festival in Hollywood, where she is also set to receive the MIFF Icon Award, making the celebration an even bigger showcase of Filipino excellence.

Malaysia brings language and food diplomacy to UP students. Language and food offered two different ways of understanding Malaysia as the country’s embassy in Manila welcomed students and faculty from the University of the Philippines Diliman for an afternoon of cultural exchange. The Food and Language Sharing Session brought 24 students studying Bahasa Melayu at UP Diliman’s Department of Linguistics to the Malaysian Embassy, where lessons moved beyond the classroom and into conversation, cuisine, and shared Southeast Asian traditions. The delegation was led by Department of Linguistics Chair Professor Francisco C. Rosario Jr., together with faculty members Professor Divine Angeli P. Endriga, Therese Maria Abigail V. Ledesma, and Katrina Joyce S. Jose. The program grew out of discussions between Malaysia’s Ambassador Dato’ Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino and UP representatives in June on expanding educational and cultural cooperation between the two countries. Welcoming the students with a traditional pantun, Ambassador Castelino underscored how learning another country’s language can lead to a deeper appreciation of its people and culture. “Language opens the door to understanding, while food reveals the heart of a culture,” he said. “Our shared Southeast Asian heritage reminds us that, despite differences in language, our traditions and hospitality continue to unite us.” The afternoon put that idea into practice. Embassy chef Ammar Syafiq bin Ayob, or Chef Ammar, demonstrated how to prepare “Mee Hailam” while introducing students to Malaysian culinary traditions. The menu extended to other familiar Malaysian favorites, including “Nasi Lemak Ayam Berempah,” “Teh Tarik,” and “Kek Batik,” giving participants another vocabulary through which to experience the country. Students also put their Bahasa Melayu skills to the test through a quiz on language and culture, with winners receiving prizes featuring Wira and Manja, the mascots of Visit Malaysia Year 2026. Beyond the afternoon’s lighter moments, the initiative reflected a larger diplomatic purpose. Bahasa Melayu is spoken across Southeast Asia, and encouraging its study among Filipino students creates another avenue for greater engagement not only with Malaysia, but with the wider ASEAN community. Ambassador Castelino expressed hope that the partnership with UP Diliman would continue, encouraging students to regard the embassy as a space where they could practice the language and deepen their understanding of Malaysia.

Lawyers ask SC to allow all courts to use Filipino language during hearings from August 1-31. The Supreme Court (SC) was asked anew to direct all courts in the country to use Filipino, the national language, in all proceedings during the celebration of the National Language Month on August 1 to 31. The plea was earlier aired by the Philippine Trial Lawyers Association, Inc. (PTLA) in a letter sent to Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo by the group’s president Atty. Pete S. Principe. The SC’s full court session is on July 29, three days before the start of the national language celebration in the country. The PTLA had earlier adopted a resolution to urge the SC to use Filipino during the month-long celebration. The resolution was attached to the PLTA’s letter sent to Chief Justice Gesmundo. The yearly celebration of the National Language Month is mandated under Proclamation No. 1041 issued by then president Fidel V. Ramos. The lawyers’ group said its request is in line with the government’s push for the strong use of Filipino language to strengthen the economic programs of the government. It noted that President Marcos himself has been using Filipino in his official meetings and instructions as well as in his speeches nationwide since 92 percent of Filipinos can fully understand and speak the Filipino language. “Tagalog is the nucleus of Filipino National Language and is known as the major native tongue and widely recognized as the leading language out of around 176 languages all over the country,” Principe said. He also recalled that Chief Justice Gesmundo used the Filipino language in his speech in Caloocan City when he was keynote speaker during the 2026 Independence Day celebration and during his speech at the 18th Graduation Ceremony of Bulacan State University Law School. At the same time, the PTLA noted that Associate Justice Ramon Paul L. Hernando was warmly applauded by delivering a speech mixed with Tagalog during the 20th Graduation Ceremony of the Bulacan State University Law School. PTLA Secretary General Atty. Yolando F. Lim, on the other hand, noted that Filipino is also dominantly used in the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte before the Senate sitting as Impeachment Court. “Noticeably, viewers are now strongly hooked on TV due to the very effective use of Tagalog by the prosecution and the defense panels. Even the Senator Judges switch Tagalog and English effectively for the benefit of the public,” Lim said. The PTLA cited that the use of the Filipino language is in line with Article XIV, Sections 6 to 9 of the Constitution. It said that Section 6 specifically states that the national language of the Philippines is Filipino. while Section 7 provides that “for purposes of communication and instruction, the official languages of the Philippines are Filipino and, until otherwise provided by law, English.” It also said that Section 8 states that the “Constitution shall be promulgated in Filipino and English and shall be translated into major regional languages, Arabic, and Spanish,” while Section 9 mandates Congress to “establish a national language commission composed of representatives of various regions and disciplines which shall undertake, coordinate, and promote researches for the development, propagation, and preservation of Filipino and other languages.”

Robin Padilla brushes off Angel Locsin's remarks: 'Baka may pinagdadaanan'. Robin Padilla has finally addressed Angel Locsin's open letter criticizing his political views, but instead of firing back, the actor-turned-senator said he chose understanding over confrontation. Speaking in an interview with Sonshine Media Network International (SMNI), Padilla said he and wife Mariel Padilla decided against responding publicly because they consider Locsin a friend. "Baka may pinagdadaanan si Angel… intindihin na lang natin. Huwag na kaming sumagot o magsalita," he said, adding that his lines remain open should the actress want to talk. Padilla also responded to Locsin's reference to his past association with leftist ideology, clarifying that while he still identifies with its ideals, he draws a clear line between political beliefs and armed struggle. Recalling how he became close to Locsin through their shared interest in martial arts, Padilla said he had been upfront about his political leanings. "Wala namang masama kung leftist ka. Ang masama ay kung ikaw ay may dalang baril," he said. Locsin's open letter drew support from several personalities, including Anne Curtis, Enchong Dee, Bea Binene, and Marina Summers. Padilla, meanwhile, received public backing from his brother, actor Rommel Padilla. In her letter, Locsin urged Padilla to use his platform more responsibly, saying public officials should be held to a higher standard because their words carry weight. She also expressed disappointment over what she described as his repeated controversial remarks, writing that she missed "the Robin Padilla who stood up for the oppressed and fought for what he believed was right." Despite the criticism, Padilla maintained there was no ill will toward the actress, saying he would rather understand her situation than engage in a public exchange. As of writing, neither Locsin nor Padilla has issued further statements on the matter.

FASHION PULIS: Negativity galore. Over the past few weeks, Talented Actress (TA) has been the subject of numerous negative write-ups. Looking back, TA's career began amid controversy, one that was never acknowledged by the alleged culprit or her home studio. Nonetheless, the issue prompted TA to transfer to another network. Years later, TA steadily climbed the ladder of success. In her new home, she got the breaks she needed and eventually became a household name. Along the way, she formed lasting friendships as her popularity grew. She was also given opportunities to showcase her talents, proving she was much more than just a pretty face. As she navigated life's twists and turns, TA found love and even considered leaving everything behind for the sake of the right person. Sadly, she was not destined to settle down, and she eventually decided to come home. Opportunities still awaited her, but things may have changed. "It was not her story to tell," sources claimed. But she allegedly shared it anyway, and the incident supposedly damaged her relationship with CF. "Everything negative — pressure, challenges — is all an opportunity for me to rise." — Kobe Bryant Nonchalant acceptance When a group of netizens decided to have a meal at a restaurant in an upscale mall, little did they know they were about to witness a memorable encounter with Ageless Actress (AA). The friends had planned a quiet get-together, but their lunch was interrupted by AA's animated conversation with her amigas.
