Filipino architecture student wins global competition with design for Sama-Bajau community. As an archipelago, the Philippines has long struggled to ensure that every community receives equal opportunities and attention. Those living on the margins are often left out of conversations about development. But many young Filipinos are beginning to challenge that reality by using their talents to bring overlooked stories into the spotlight. For Ejhey Durias, an architecture student from the University of Mindanao, that meant designing not for skyscrapers or luxury developments, but for a community whose way of life is slowly disappearing. His project, Banuas Lawod, earned the highest global recognition at the AYDA Awards, an international design competition for students, by tackling the decline of aquaculture and the displacement of coastal communities. The proposal was inspired by the Sama-Bajau community of Adecor in the Island Garden City of Samal. Once known as sea nomads with a deep connection to the ocean, many members of the community have been pushed inland by rapid urbanization, threatening not only their livelihood but also their culture and identity. Instead of treating architecture as simply the creation of buildings, Ejhey designed a holistic aquaculture community hub where displaced families can reconnect with the sea. His proposal combines Lepa-inspired housing with a tide-responsive layout surrounding a communal space, while a metabolic aquaculture hub allows fish, shellfish, and seaweed to thrive in a sustainable, closed-loop system. For the young designer, the project was driven by a desire to tell stories that often go unheard. "One thing that truly inspired me to pursue the project, Banuas Lawod, was my desire to become a voice for the unheard, communities whose stories are often neglected and overlooked," he told Manila Bulletin Lifestyle. As he researched the decline of aquaculture, he also learned about the struggles that forced many coastal families away from the waters that once sustained them. "I realized these issues affect not only livelihoods but also culture and identity," he said. "Our oceans are part of our identity, and protecting them means protecting the communities that depend on them." His approach also challenged the idea that innovation must replace tradition. "Innovation should not reject culture and tradition. It should strengthen it," Ejhey said. Before creating the design, he spent time studying the community's way of life, traditions, and relationship with the sea. Every architectural decision, he said, was made to respect their identity while creating opportunities for a better future. Winning the global award came as a surprise. "It honestly took a few minutes, even days, for it to sink in," he shared. "I felt very proud to represent not only my university but the entire Philippines on the global stage." The recognition also earned him a fully funded fellowship at the Harvard Graduate School of Design, where he hopes to learn from designers around the world and bring those lessons back to the Philippines to create projects with meaningful impact. For fellow young designers, Ejhey believes that creating socially relevant work begins long before the first sketch. "It all starts with listening," he said. "When we design with empathy and purpose, architecture becomes more than just creating beautiful spaces. It becomes a way to genuinely improve people's lives." As he looks ahead, Ejhey hopes to continue creating designs that celebrate Filipino culture while addressing the needs of vulnerable communities. For him, architecture is not only about shaping spaces, but also about helping people reconnect with the identities and traditions that make those spaces worth preserving.

3 hurt as rockslide hits Montalban homes; residents told to stay alert. Three people, including two children, were injured when a rockslide struck homes in Sitio Kayrupa, Barangay San Rafael, Montalban, Rizal, on Friday night, July 24. The Barangay San Rafael said the injured residents were immediately given first aid by the Barangay Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (BDRRMO) and transported to Ynares Hospital for further medical treatment. It said four houses in the Bangkaan area were damaged by the rockslide. Barangay Captain Judith Cruz and other barangay officials immediately went to the area to check on the affected families, ensure their safety, and lead the response to the incident. “Nagpapasalamat po ako sa Panginoon at kahit malalaking Bato ang bumaksak galing sa bundok walang malubhang nasaktan sa mga ka-Barangay ko (I thank the Lord that even though large rocks fell from the mountain, none of my fellow barangay residents were seriously injured),” Cruz said in a Facebook post. Following the incident and amid continuous rains, the barangay urged residents, especially those living near mountains, slopes, and riverbanks, to stay alert for possible hazards. “Kung mapansin ang pagguho ng lupa, pagbiyak ng lupa, pagbagsak ng mga bato, o anumang senyales ng panganib, lumikas agad sa ligtas na lugar at makipag-ugnayan sa ating command center o sa pinakamalapit na opisyal ng barangay (If you notice ground movement, ground cracks, falling rocks, or any other signs of danger, immediately evacuate to a safe area and contact our command center or the nearest barangay official),” it said.

BFP goes digital, holds ‘e-hire’ system for fire officer applicants. From the traditional pen-and-paper format, the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) has now gone online with the pioneer “E-Hire recruitment’’ process and conduct of its first “Digitalized Qualifying Examination. Under the modernized scheme, a total of 7,913 Fire Officer 1 (FO1) applicants nationwide completed their digital examination on July 23, speeding up the recruitment process and ensuring that all tests are scored fairly and accurately. BFP officer-on-charge (OIC) Chief Supt. Wilberto Rico Neil Kwan Tiu said that the conduct of the digital examination was coursed through and facilitated by the bureau’s regional offices. Highlighting the changes from previous recruitment cycles, Kwan Tiu noted that the “digital exam’’ allows applicants to view their results immediately after the examination. He noted that the modernized examination shift aids the BFP in further promoting transparency and speeding up the entire recruitment cycle for the FO1 applicants “Through this innovation, we make sure that the hiring is based on merit and fitness, and the process is fast and fair for everyone," Kwan Tiu pointed out. “Applicants who have passed the qualifying exam and have been included in the quota (based on maximum candidate pool or 200 percent of the quota of qualified applicants) due to their ranking will move forward to the next step as per BFP Memorandum Circular 2026-015,’’ Kwant Tiu explained. “They are also advised to regularly monitor the official social media channels of their respective BFP Regional Offices for further updates and announcements,’’ he continued.

'Kiyapo' exits PAR, Signal No. 1 stays as habagat brings heavy rains—PAGASA. Typhoon Kiyapo has exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR), but storm signal number1 remains in effect over several areas as the cyclone and the enhanced southwest monsoon continue to bring strong winds and heavy rains, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Saturday, July 25. PAGASA weather specialist Veronica Torres said Kiyapo left the country’s area of responsibility at around 2 a.m. and now bears its international name, “Noul.” “Itong si Bagyong Kiyapo ay lumabas na ng ating Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) kaninang alas dos ng madaling araw. Ito ay may international name na ‘Noul’. Ngayon ay nasa Typhoon category na itong si Bagyong Kiyapo (Typhoon Kiyapo exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) at around 2 a.m. today. It now carries the international name ‘Noul.’ It has intensified into the typhoon category),” Torres said. As of 4 a.m., PAGASA said the typhoon was located 320 kilometers west of Basco, Batanes, with maximum sustained winds of 120 kilometers per hour (kph) near the center and gusts of up to 150 kph. It was moving west northwest at 25 kph. The weather specialist said Kiyapo is forecast to continue moving northwestward before making landfall over southern mainland China. “Inaasahan natin na tatahakin nito ang direksyong northwest bago mag-landfall sa may southern mainland China. Due to favorable conditions, posible itong lumakas pa in the next 12 hours, although papalayo naman ito sa ating bansa. Once na ito ay mag-landfall, inaasahan na ’yung tuluyan pa niyang paghina (It is expected to move northwestward before making landfall over southern mainland China. Due to favorable conditions, it may still intensify within the next 12 hours, although it is already moving away from the Philippines. Once it makes landfall, it is expected to weaken steadily),” she said. Despite the cyclone’s exit from PAR, PAGASA maintained TCWS No. 1 over Batanes, the Babuyan Islands, the northwestern portion of mainland Cagayan, Ilocos Norte, and the northern portion of Apayao. “Kahit nakalabas na sa ating PAR itong mino-monitor nating bagyo, meron parin tayong nakataas na Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal: Signal No. 1 sa may Batanes, Babuyan Islands, sa may northwestern portion ng mainland Cagayan, sa may Ilocos Norte, at sa northern portion din ng Apayao (Although the tropical cyclone we have been monitoring has already exited the Philippine Area of Responsibility, Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 1 remains in effect over Batanes, the Babuyan Islands, the northwestern portion of mainland Cagayan, Ilocos Norte, and the northern portion of Apayao),” said Torres. The state weather bureau said the combined effects of Kiyapo’s outer circulation and the enhanced southwest monsoon, locally known as habagat, will continue to bring strong winds across several parts of the country. According to PAGASA, strong wind gusts will prevail on Saturday across most of Luzon, Western Visayas, the Negros Island Region, Northern Samar, Zamboanga del Norte, and Davao Oriental. By Sunday, gusty conditions are forecast over Batanes, Cagayan, the Ilocos Region, Zambales, Bataan, Quezon, and the Mimaropa region, it added.

Palestinian caught stealing money bag at QC hotel café. A 36-year-old Palestinian man was arrested after allegedly taking a money bag containing P5,020 and an empty cash box from a hotel café on Timog Avenue in Barangay South Triangle, Quezon City, at around 11:06 p.m. on Thursday, July 23. The suspect, identified as “Ham,” was intercepted by hotel security personnel at the establishment’s exit after the incident was detected through the hotel’s CCTV monitoring system. Initial investigation showed that the suspect entered the café and allegedly took the money bag and empty cash box without the knowledge or consent of the 24-year-old male cashier. Recovered from the suspect were P5,020 in various peso bills and coins, the cash bag, the empty cash box, and a backpack. Personnel of Kamuning Police Station (PS 10) later responded and took custody of the suspect from the hotel security personnel. Further verification showed that the suspect had previous criminal records for estafa, unjust vexation, resistance and disobedience to a person in authority, use of a fictitious name, and concealing his true name in October 2025, as well as theft in May 2026. The suspect will be charged with theft before the Quezon City Prosecutor’s Office.

Kelsey Merritt, Chace Crawford reportedly split after more than a year together. Filipina model Kelsey Merritt and American actor Chace Crawford have reportedly ended their relationship after more than a year together. According to People magazine, a source confirmed that the couple had gone their separate ways. Neither Merritt nor Crawford has publicly addressed the report, and representatives for both did not respond to the publication's requests for comment. Rumors of a romance first surfaced in January 2025 when the pair were photographed having coffee together in California. Their relationship drew wider attention three months later after they were seen sharing a kiss while in New York City. Over the following months, the two made several public appearances together, including attending the 2025 US Open Women's Singles final. They were also spotted enjoying a virtual golf outing and were seen celebrating each other's birthdays, fueling speculation that their relationship had grown more serious. Despite the public interest, both Merritt and Crawford largely kept their romance out of the spotlight, rarely commenting on their relationship in interviews or on social media. Crawford, 40, is best known for portraying Nate Archibald in the hit teen drama "Gossip Girl" and currently stars in the superhero series "The Boys." Merritt, meanwhile, made history as the first Filipina to walk in the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show after joining the brand's roster of models in 2018. She has since established herself as one of the country's most recognizable international fashion figures, working with leading luxury and lifestyle brands.

Golden Tigresses, Lady Blazers battle for crown. Games Sunday: (Playtime FilOil Arena) 2 p.m. --- Letran vs Southern Storm 4 p.m. --- UST vs CSB University of Santo Tomas and College of Saint Benilde battle for supremacy in an exciting winner-take-all 2026 Shakey’s Collegiate National Invitationals title showdown on Sunday, July 26, at the Playtime FilOil Arena in San Juan. After a grueling race to the biggest stage, the unbeaten Golden Tigresses and the equally formidable Lady Blazers meet one last time for all the marbles at 4 p.m. Meanwhile, Letran and Australian guest team Southern Storm Melbourne will be squaring off in the 2 p.m. battle for third to salvage a podium finish. UST has its sights trained on completing an amazing sweep of the weeklong competition backed by Shakey’s Pizza Parlor, Peri-Peri Charcoal Chicken, Potato Corner, and R and B Milk Tea. The Tigresses booted out Letran, 25-10, 25-19, 25-12, in the knockout semifinals last Friday for their sixth straight win in as many starts and a breakthrough championship appearance. UST’s highest result in the previous editions of the tournament supported by Jetour, Baic, Eurotel, Victory Liner Rent & Go, F2 Logistics, Summit Natural Drinking Water, PusoP.com and Smart Sports was a third-place finish in 2023. Veterans Regina Jurado, Angge Poyos, Marga Altea and Avril Bron alongside young guns Kim Rubin and Ashley Dianne Knop banner the Shaq Delos Santos-mentored Tigresses, who are looking for a fitting follow-up to their high school counterpart’s Shakey’s Girls Volleyball Invitational League Rising Stars Cup and Juniors National Invitationals title conquests. “Gusto lang din naming matuloy 'yung streak ng UST sa Shakey’s championship. Siguro 'yun din talaga ang goal namin na makuha 'yung finals this Sunday,” Jurado said. UST defeated CSB, 25-22, 25-15, 15-25, 25-12, in their elimination round meeting last Monday. On the other hand, the Lady Blazers are clinging to the momentum they built after their lone setback to pull off a shocker over the mighty Tigresses. Kailangan naming mas tapangan pa sa floor defense, kasi knowing UST, maraming malalakas pumalo sa kanila. Magaganda rin 'yung placement nila and actually sa blockings din,” Bartolome said. “So, challenge na lang din ito sa amin kung paano namin sila lalabanan,” she added. CSB, which handed UST its only set loss so far in the competition, seeks to settle unfinished business following a runner-up finish in the tournament’s Luzon leg last year. All games in the competition, backed by technical partners Philippine Sports Commission, Commission on Higher Education, Mikasa, Asics, Rigour Technology and Team Rebel Sports, are available live and on-demand via PusoP.com livestream and Solar Sports.

Grigsby gets passing mark but Cone not closing doors on Brownlee. Barangay Ginebra head coach Tim Cone was pretty much satisfied with new import Riley Grigsby through the first two games that he played but he insisted that the team isn’t fully closing its door on a possible return for Justin Brownlee. The veteran mentor was impressed with the 26-year-old forward, who has been doing great in filling in the shoes of the Ginebra resident import. Grigsby made head turns in his first game, exploding for 42 points although the Kings lost, 78-81, to Phoenix. In his second game – a 115-85 win over Blackwater, he only finished with 18 points but did a little bit of everything after also compiling eight rebounds, five assists, two steals and a block. “We didn't give him a lot of help in the first game and he kind of took it upon himself to keep us in the game. And today, he came in, we talked about it, again, ball movement and moving the people and he really stuck to that,” Cone said of Grigsby. “He stuck to what we wanted him to do. And he's showing us that he's special that way. Follow game plans, working behind the defense, he'll go to the boards, he'll do all the dirty work,” he added. “It's not about how talented he is, it's how well he fits us. And right now he's proven to fit us very well.” Even with Grigsby doing well, however, Cone stressed that the door remained open for a possible return for Brownlee, especially whenever he’s ready and back on his top shape. And Grigsby is very much aware of the situation. “We are not putting anything in stone but I think we owe it to Justin from a loyalty standpoint that when he is ready, he is going to play,” said Cone. “The longer Justin has to recuperate and get back, the better it is. We were very clear with Riley that he's coming with eyes wide open. He knows that he's following up the GOAT, and it's a tough thing to do and he seems to have the perfect character to do that. But he's coming with eyes wide open.”

'STRONGER': Joey Albert on finding hope, courage, and faith amid cancer battle. Singer Joey Albert has spent more than four decades inspiring audiences with her music, but the greatest lesson she has ever shared did not come from a song. It came from surviving cancer. Looking back on her battle with both cervical and colon cancer, Albert spoke candidly about the fear, uncertainty, and emotional toll of the disease, while offering a message of hope to others facing the same fight. In an interview with Boy Abunda, the singer admitted that confronting cancer meant learning to live one day at a time. "You know it's just really one foot in front of the other when it's something like that and hope and faith," she said. Albert revealed that the diagnosis was devastating but not entirely unexpected. Having watched both her father and sister succumb to cancer, she had long prepared herself for the possibility that she, too, might one day hear the same life-changing words. "Parang half of you expects it already na mangyayari ito sa akin. Nung finally nangyari na sa akin, actually tuwing nangyayari iisipin mo, 'ito na ba Lord?'" she recalled. Rather than allowing fear to consume her, Albert said she focused on making every day count, ensuring every decision she made would benefit her family and the people who had stood by her throughout her career. "Sinubukan ko talaga at sinikap kong gawin decision para sa kabutihan ng pamilya ko, ng mga anak ko, asawa ko, or ng mga naniwala sa akin throughout my career." Her battle was marked not only by chemotherapy and the physical effects of treatment, including hair loss, but also by the emotional burden that many cancer patients know all too well: living with uncertainty. "It's also the uncertainty. Of course, yes laban ka ng laban pero hindi mo rin naman talaga alam kung hanggang saan ka dadalhin nung paglalaban mo. Although, courage lang." Courage did not mean pretending she was unafraid. It meant choosing to keep moving forward despite not knowing what the future held. Cancer changed her perspective on life. Instead of questioning her faith, the illness strengthened it and taught her the importance of caring for herself. "Nung nagka-cancer na ko, parang that's when I realized kailangan matuto akong mahalin sarili ko na pag wala ako, wala rin naman akong magagawa para sa iba." Albert believes suffering can also become a source of compassion and purpose. "Ang tinuro sa akin, yung mga paghihirap natin, puwede nating gawing mga tulay, stepping stones, para ipagdasal ang ibang tao. Kasi yun yung pinakamahalagang maalay natin sa Panginoon yung pain. Sacrifice is the most beautiful gift we can offer to God for other people." Her story is one that resonates beyond show business. For countless people battling cancer, Albert's journey serves as a reminder that fear is natural, but hope, faith, and the support of loved ones can help carry them through even the darkest moments. Now cancer-free and embracing life with renewed gratitude, Albert is preparing to celebrate another milestone, this time on stage. The veteran singer returns to the spotlight with "Fortyfied: Joey Albert 45" set for July 30 at the Newport Performing Arts Theater in Pasay City.

Centeno, Amit in Last 16 of world 8-ball tilt. Chezka Centeno and Rubilen Amit took contrasting paths to reach the Last 16 of the 2026 Oneida WPA Women’s 8-Ball World Championships in Green Bay, Wisconsin on Friday, July 24. Centeno, last year’s finalist, stamped her class with dominant victories over Ada Lio of the United States, 7-2; Eylul Kibaroglu of Turkey, 7-3; and Seo Seoa of South Korea, 7-5, to cruise into the knockout stage. Amit, meanwhile, had to battle through the one-loss side after opening her campaign with a win by forfeit over Egypt’s Salma Shaheen. The Filipina veteran followed it up with a convincing 7-3 triumph over hometown bet Savannah Easton before absorbing a 5-7 setback to Chinese Taipei’s Wei Tzu-Chien that sent her to the losers’ bracket. The 44-year-old Cebuana, still chasing the elusive world 8-ball title to complete her collection after conquering the 9-ball and 10-ball disciplines, quickly regained her form by routing Canada’s Brittany Bryant, 7-3, to join Centeno in the Round of 16. Amit will next take on American Sofia Mast, while Centeno faces defending champion Jasmin Ouschan in a rematch of last year's final, where the Austrian edged the Zamboanga standout, 9-8. Should both Filipinas emerge victorious, they will set up an all-Filipino quarterfinal showdown.

Speaker Dy confident Senate can do lawmaking on top of impeachment trial duties. Despite its daunting task, House Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III expressed confidence that the Senate can simultaneously fulfill its constitutional duty as an impeachment court while continuing its legislative responsibilities. Dy had this say over the weekend, as lawmakers from both legislative chambers anticpate the opening of the second regular session of the 20th Congress on Monday, July 27, the same day as President Marcos' fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA). The Speaker from Isabela's 6th district said the House was prepared to work closely with the Senate under the leadership of Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian to complete the remaining priority legislation, particularly those identified by the Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council (LEDAC). “May kumpiyansa po kami na may kakayahan ang Senado na pagsabayin ang kanilang constitutional duty bilang impeachment court at ang kanilang tungkulin bilang mga mambabatas,” Dy said. (We are confident that the Senate has the capacity to fulfill its constitutional duty as an impeachment court while also carrying out its role as legislators.) He added that both chambers can continue refining measures through bicameral conference committees and technical working groups. “Handa po ang Kongreso na makipagtulungan sa Senado sa pamumuno ni Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian... nang sa gayon ay makagawa tayo ng mga batas na napapanahon at tutugon sa pangangailangan ng ating mga kababayan.” (Congress is ready to work with the Senate under the leadership of Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian… so that we can craft laws that are timely and responsive to the needs of our people.) Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial--where senators serve as senator-judges--began last July 6. Gatchalian had earlier estimated that the proceedings could last seven to eight months. The House has a part in the trial too, as it has sent a team of 11 solon-prosecutors to gain a conviction from the respondent, Duterte. Dy said the focus in the second regular session should remain on delivering meaningful legislation. “Inaasahan po nating magkakaisa ang dalawang Kapulungan upang mapanatili ang momentum ng ating legislative agenda.” (We expect both Chambers to unite in order to sustain the momentum of our legislative agenda.) “Sa dulo ng lahat ng ito, hindi naman ito tungkol sa Kamara o Senado. Ang mahalaga ay magkaroon tayo ng mga batas na magpapagaan ng buhay ng ating mga kababayan at magpapaunlad sa ating bansa," the House leader said. (In the end, this is not about the House or the Senate.What matters is that we enact laws that will ease the lives of our people and advance our nation.) During the first regular session, the House managed to pass 26 out of the 52 LEDAC measures. Among the measures are the landmark Right to Information Act, the Anti-Political Dynasty Act, reforms to the Bank Deposits Secrecy Law, and the law resetting the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections.

'No more crossing rivers': Aquino hails new law improving education access in GIDA communities. Senator Bam Aquino has hailed the signing into law of a measure designed to improve access to education in Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDA), saying it will help remove long-standing barriers that prevent children in remote communities from attending school safely. Aquino, who chairs the Senate Committee on Basic Education, was the principal sponsor and co-author of Republic Act No. 12321, or the Last Mile and GIDA Schools Act, which President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. recently signed into law. The measure is Aquino's first enacted law since returning to the Senate in 2025. “Ang pagsasabatas nito ay isang mahalagang hakbang para matiyak na walang magiging hadlang sa bawat batang Pilipino na makapag-aral, kahit saan man siyang dako ng Pilipinas (The enactment of this law is a significant step toward ensuring that no Filipino child faces barriers to education, no matter where they live in the country),” Aquino said. “Sa tulong nito, umaasa tayong matutuldukan na ang mga sitwasyon na kailangang lumusong sa ilog, maglakad ng ilang kilometro sa gitna ng init, at tumawid sa mga sira-sirang tulay ang ating mga estudyante bago makarating sa paaralan (With this law, we hope to put an end to situations where our students have to wade through rivers, walk several kilometers under the scorching sun, and cross dilapidated bridges just to get to school),” he added. The new law sets accessibility standards requiring schools to be within a three-kilometer walking distance of students or to have safe public transportation available. It also requires the government to improve school facilities by constructing adequate classrooms and ensuring access to essential services such as roads, electricity, water, and internet connectivity through stronger interagency coordination. In addition, the measure provides incentives for teachers assigned to far-flung communities, including additional pay and allowances, transportation and housing assistance, and opportunities for continued professional development to improve teacher retention. The law also prioritizes the recruitment of qualified teachers and school personnel who either come from, are willing to live in, or have cultural ties to GIDA communities, with the aim of strengthening engagement between educators and students.

PCSO completes nationwide patient transport vehicle rollout. All 82 provinces in the Philippines now have Patient Transport Vehicles (PTVs) from the Philippine Charity Sweepstakes Office (PCSO) after the agency completed its nationwide distribution program on Friday, July 24. This was achieved following the turnover of the final batch of 34 PTV units during a ceremony at the Provincial Capitol of Pampanga, covering the remaining provinces in Regions I, II, III, and the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR), and completing the agency’s nationwide provincial rollout. “The milestone marks the full implementation of one of the Marcos administration's flagship healthcare initiatives, ensuring that every province in the country now has dedicated PTVs to strengthen emergency medical response and improve access to healthcare services,” PCSO said. According to the agency, the nationwide rollout is the first in Philippine history to equip all provinces with ambulances under a government-led program. “PCSO’s provincial rollout builds on another major achievement of the agency after it attained 100% distribution of PTVs to all cities and municipalities nationwide in early December 2025,” it said in a statement. The agency said the completion of the provincial rollout brings the total number PTVs distributed nationwide to 1,830. PCSO General Manager Melquiades A. Robles said the successful completion of the nationwide provincial rollout carries out President Marcos’ directive to ensure that emergency medical assistance is more accessible to every Filipino. "This mission is guided by the vision of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. that no Filipino, no matter how far or how humble their circumstances, should ever be left without access to emergency medical care,” he said. Robles said the nationwide provincial rollout of PTVs reflects the government’s commitment to improving access to emergency medical services. “With the distribution of the 34 PTVs today, PCSO has completed a nationwide total of 164 provincial Patient Transport Vehicles distributed under the program,” the agency said. The agency said the PTVs are meant to provide safe and timely transport for patients in need of immediate medical attention, enabling local governments to improve emergency response and expedite transfers to appropriate healthcare facilities.

Harry Roque’s asylum bid in Austria denied, Jonvic says. Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Juanito Victor “Jonvic’’ Remulla confirmed that the asylum application of former presidential spokesman Harry Roque in Austria was rejected. With the failed Vienna asylum bid, Remulla said authorities are just waiting for the Interpol Red Notice and at anytime Roque can be brought back to the country, “at the shortest time possible.’’ “Nasa Vienna (capital of Austria) siya (Harry Roque). Meron na kaming communication, so hindi siya nagtatago but anytime pwede na namin siyang kunin. Ah human trafficking ang kaso niya. (He is in Vienna. We already have a communication, he is not hiding but anytime we can get him. He has a human trafficking case),’’ Remulla noted. But things seemed easier said than done even with Remulla’s optimism of Roque’s repatriation, admitting facing legal human rights obstacles in Europe. “Europe is very particular sa human rights, very procedural sila, they throw roadblocks along the way (Europe is very particular on human rights, they are very procedural, they throw roadblocks along the way),’’ Remulla explained. Since Roque entered Europe using a Schengen visa issued by Austria, it is Austria that must decide on his asylum petition. Under the Dublin rules, the country that issued a person’s visa is usually responsible for handling their asylum application. In a Facebook Live broadcast earlier, Roque confirmed that the Dutch Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) denied both his initial petition and appeal for asylum in the Netherlands. Roque is at the center of a human trafficking case linked to a Philippine Offshore Gaming Operator (POGO) hub in Porac, Pampanga. In May 2025, the Angeles Regional Trial Court issued arrest warrants against Roque, businesswoman Cassandra Ong and 50 others for alleged involvement in human trafficking connected to the Lucky South 99 POGO hub. With the case drawing worldwide attention, Roque was also implicated for his active role in securing the POGO’s license and managing legal matters for the firm.

Why The Spirits Library belongs on Asia's Best Bars list. Straight off its newly minted inclusion in Asia's 50 Best Bars 51-100 list, we made our way last July 15 to one of Manila's nightlife hotspots, Poblacion in Makati, to revisit The Spirits Library. As if earning a place on one of the region's most prestigious bar rankings wasn't reason enough to stop by, the bar happened to be hosting 2025 Diageo World Class Bartender of the Year Felice Capasso for a one-night guest shift, giving patrons the rare opportunity to sample cocktails prepared by one of the world's best. I've had my share of memorable cocktails over the years, but it isn't often that you get to watch someone of Felice's caliber at work. There was no unnecessary flair or theatrics behind the bar. Every bottle, every stir, every garnish, and every pour had a purpose. It didn't take long to understand why he is regarded as one of the industry's best. For the evening, Felice presented five cocktails inspired by Nordic flavors, each showcasing one of three Diageo spirits: The Singleton single malt Scotch whisky, Don Julio Blanco tequila, and Tanqueray No. TEN gin. Instead of burying the base spirit beneath layers of ingredients, the drinks allowed each label's character to come through, proving that sometimes restraint leaves the biggest impression. Among the lineup, two cocktails immediately stood out. The Negroni was everything the classic should be—balanced, aromatic, and remarkably clean, while allowing the citrus character of Tanqueray No. TEN to remain front and center. Just as memorable was the Strawberry cocktail, where ripe fruit complemented the smooth richness of The Singleton without overwhelming it. They were very different drinks, yet both reflected the same philosophy: Understanding the spirit first, then building around it. That, Felice explained, is where every great cocktail begins. "It's not about what you do, but how you do it," he said to us. "Besides the technical aspect, which of course requires years of learning, it's ultimately about the way the drink is delivered and the experience you create for your guest." For him, creativity comes only after understanding the fundamentals. "The approaches are almost unlimited," he explained. "The first step is to understand what guides each spirit, then identify one or two of its defining characteristics, whether that's texture, aroma, or flavor, and build your concept around them." He compared bartending to cooking, arguing that the world's best bartenders should know their ingredients just as intimately as accomplished chefs. "Have you ever met a great chef who doesn't know the DNA of the raw materials they're working with?" he asked. "Every great chef understands them in detail." The same principle applies behind the bar, he said. Bartenders should understand what gives a spirit its character before deciding how to present it in a cocktail. "It's science. Your job as a professional is to understand those factors and then decide how to highlight them in the cocktail." Those ideas became the focus of an exclusive masterclass Felice conducted for Filipino bartenders the following day. Rather than concentrating on recipes alone, he challenged participants to stay curious, keep learning, and deepen their understanding of the craft. "Winning World Class is not the end. It's the beginning," he said. "Knowledge is power. World Class pushes you to perform under pressure, to research, to study, and to work against deadlines. When you sign up for World Class, you learn more in a few months than you probably did in years." The guest shift came at an exciting time for The Spirits Library. Fresh off its recognition by Asia's 50 Best Bars, the Poblacion destination continues to cement its place among the country's leading cocktail bars. Awards may draw first-time visitors, but it's experiences like this that keep people coming back.

More than 200,000 people flee raging wildfires in France and Spain, some escaping by boat. ARCACHON, France (AP) — Massive forest fires forced the evacuation of some 200,000 people in southwestern France and central Spain on Friday, with residents fleeing towns near Madrid and Bordeaux as the flames raged out of control. Firefighters and authorities in both European countries were caught off guard by the virulence of the fires, which were fueled by high temperatures and the long-term effects of climate change. Firefighters in Spain admitted the fires were so fast and violent that they could not be tackled head on. Some people even fled by boat when flames swept through the touristic area on France’s Atlantic coast. Some 141,000 fled homes in the Gironde and Landes departments in France, the French interior ministry said. In central Spain, 60,000 were forced from their homes, according to the Spanish interior ministry. Dozens of French firefighters were injured, authorities said, but no deaths were reported in either country despite the scenes of panic as townsfolk fled by car and police went door to door to tell people to leave as large plumes of smoke rose from the neighboring woodlands. Wildfire headed toward Bordeaux France’s Interior minister Laurent Nunez said that the large wildfire that ravaged large swaths of land in southwestern France is heading toward the city of Bordeaux. Speaking to French TV channel Tf1, Nunez said the wildfire that earlier in the day forced the evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula has swept across 140 square kilometers, with 110,000 people fleeing their homes in the Gironde region. “We learned in the middle of the afternoon that, following the wind shift, it had become a large, self-sustaining fire that is extremely difficult to bring under control,” Nunez said. “It is now moving east, toward the Bordeaux metropolitan area. We are going to reorganize our response so we can fight it from the ground and prevent it from advancing toward Bordeaux.” Meanwhile, French President Emmanuel Macron has asked the Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to activate the government’s crisis response unit, and has instructed the armed forces to mobilize in order to provide the maximum possible reinforcement to the civilian emergency services. “This fire that we have been living with and fighting against here in Gironde for three days has reached an unprecedented magnitude," Sophie Brocas, the Nouvelle Aquitaine Prefect, said. “To combat it, we will receive extremely significant national reinforcements.” The blaze started on Wednesday near Cap Ferret peninsula on France’s Atlantic coast, located 60 kilometers (37 miles) from Bordeaux. Local authorities in the Gironde department said 53 homes and a campsite were destroyed, adding that 42 firefighters were injured. Around 1,500 people who fled the peninsula arrived by sea in the city of Arcachon, some aboard small water taxis and others on larger boats. “It’s quite impressive and even frightening," said Laurent Moretti, a resident in the town of Arès. “An evacuation on this scale has never happened before. All we really hope is that the firefighters can quickly get it under control.” A separate wildfire broke out in Landes, causing 31,000 evacuations. Authorities believe the causes of both fires in France were accidental. More than 20,000 people had already been evacuated from towns and vacation resorts on Thursday, but that number exploded on Friday as both France and Spain asked fellow European Union members for help. Macron said France will receive EU reinforcements including two Croatian Canadair firefighting aircraft, two Portuguese Air Tractor aircraft, and two heavy-lift Black Hawk helicopters from the Czech Republic and Slovakia. Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said that Italy and Greece are each sending two Canadair water-dumping airplanes, while a thousand Spanish soldiers helped firefighting efforts. Spain struggles to tackle multiple fires amid a heatwave In Spain, the government declared a national emergency for wildfires for the first time as the blazes in Madrid and the nearby province of Ávila prompted the evacuation of some 60,000 people from towns west of the capital. “I want to send a message of support to the thousands of families who face a difficult night ahead,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who will visit the fire-ravaged area on Saturday, wrote on X. The fires are being fanned by a heat wave with temperatures expected to top 39 degrees Celsius (102 Fahrenheit). Two major fires near Madrid merged into one single blaze that had quickly charred 30 square kilometers (11.5 square miles) by Friday afternoon. Regional President Isabel Díaz-Ayuso called it the worst in Madrid's history. Francisco Martín, the central government representative for the region of Madrid, said that another 20,000 people had been ordered to shelter at home. Martín said more evacuations could be coming and that the priority now was to protect the town of San Lorenzo, the home of the Escorial, Philip II's 16th-century royal palace and monastery. Meanwhile, a blaze in Ávila, less than two hours northwest of Madrid, consumed 90 square kilometers (34 square miles). Spain's Civil Guard arrested one man and is investigating another for allegedly having used heavy machinery in an area where it was prohibited for fire risk. Police believe a spark ignited the fire on Thursday. “All around the town was smoke and fire, I was scared. Everything was fire and smoke, people were nervous,” 33-year-old Joaquin Espinosa said before he and his neighbors were evacuated from the village of Chapinería. Devastating summer for fires in Spain In one week, Spain has had the worst fires on record for both the regions of Castilla La Mancha and Madrid. Firefighters were still trying to extinguish Spain’s second-largest ever fire in the Guadalajara province of Castilla La Mancha after it had destroyed some 320 square kilometers (120 square miles) over the last week. Thirteen people were also killed in a fire in southern Spain earlier this month, the deadliest fire in recent memory for Spain. Spanish Minister for the Ecological Transition Sara Aagesen said that Spain has seen 1,140 square kilometers (440 square miles) already burned this year, more than five times the burned terrain it had through the first half of 2025. Spain has experienced record temperatures in recent summers and forest fires of increasing violence. Wildfire analyst Raúl Quílez said that besides the impact of climate change, Spain’s rural areas have become more exposed to fires with the abandonment of farmlands that traditionally provided buffer zones around villages. Now, he said, trees and undergrowth often reach right to homes, putting them in harm’s way. "That makes a perfect cocktail for this type of fires,” Quílez told The Associated Press by phone from Valencia, where he works as an analyst for regional firefighters.

How Maegan Aguilar lived the painful story behind Freddie Aguilar's 'Anak'. Few songs have captured the pain of a parent watching a child lose their way quite like "Anak." Written by the late OPM legend Freddie Aguilar, the timeless classic has moved millions around the world with its haunting message about youthful rebellion, regret, and a parent's unconditional love. Freddie himself had long shared that the song was inspired by his own relationship with his parents. Decades later, life delivered a heartbreaking twist. His own daughter, singer-actress Maegan Aguilar, found herself living the very story "Anak" warned about. Born into privilege as the daughter of one of the biggest names in Original Pilipino Music, Maegan appeared destined for a successful career in entertainment. But years of addiction, pride, and poor choices slowly pulled her away from family, career, and eventually herself. Looking back during her guest appearance on "Fast Talk with Boy Abunda," Maegan candidly recounted a painful journey marked by drug addiction, repeated relapses, homelessness, and ultimately, redemption. She admitted experimenting with marijuana at just 15 years old before eventually becoming addicted to shabu. Despite receiving help from people who genuinely cared for her, including veteran singer Kuh Ledesma, Maegan repeatedly fell back into addiction. After completing her first rehabilitation program, she reunited with her then-partner, who was also using illegal drugs. "Kung isa sa amin ay gustong lumayo na sa droga or gusto nang mag-recover, pero 'yung isa, hindi pa, it's not gonna work," she explained. The relapse devastated Kuh, who had personally helped secure her rehabilitation. "She was sad. Sabi niya, 'You already know what happened to you living that life. Why do you have to repeat?'" Things only became worse. Maegan revealed she eventually became homeless, surviving for days by sleeping inside tricycles and even public restrooms. Her lowest point came outside the subdivision where her father lived. There, disheveled and under the influence of drugs, Freddie finally saw what had become of his daughter. Instead of rescuing her, he gave her perhaps the hardest lesson any father could give. "'Fix it. Ayusin mo. You don't even know how long I still have. Ayusin mo.'" At the time, Maegan admitted she misunderstood her father's refusal to save her. "I just thought he was being selfish. Kasi nga entitled ako. 'Hello, kailangan ko ng tulong, ba't 'di mo ako tulungan?' Mali." Only much later did she realize what Freddie had truly been doing. Rather than enabling her addiction, he was trusting her to find the strength to save herself. Before Freddie passed away in May 2025, Maegan managed to write him a deeply emotional letter. "'Tay, sobrang mahal niyo pala ako the whole time... Nagtiwala kayo na kakayanin ko. Nagtiwala kayo na I would find the right way.'" The two also managed to reconcile. For her birthday in April 2025, Freddie sent her a heartfelt video greeting. "'Anak, I'm so happy. I love you so much. Paglabas mo, mag-US tour tayo.'" Just a month later, he was gone. Still confined inside a rehabilitation center, Maegan was not allowed to leave to attend her father's funeral because doctors feared the emotional trauma could trigger another relapse. She was permitted to visit only briefly a week later. Now sober and reflecting on everything she had endured, Maegan said she understands why "Anak" continues to resonate across generations. "It's really about every single one of us na naging anak... Everyone's journey when they realize things." For her, the song's closing lines carry even greater meaning today. "'Pagsisisi sa isip mo, nalaman mong ika'y nagkamali...' It's not final. It's not an end. It's a continuing story." In many ways, those words became the story of her own life. Like the child in her dad's immortal masterpiece, Maegan wandered into darkness despite the love that surrounded her. Pride blinded her, addiction consumed her, and even the helping hands extended by family, friends, and mentors could not change her until she chose recovery herself. Today, having completed rehabilitation and slowly rebuilding her life, Maegan hopes to return to the entertainment industry. Her story stands as a reminder that addiction can happen to anyone, regardless of fame, privilege, or family background. More importantly, it shows that while regret may be painful, it does not have to be the final chapter. Just as "Anak" ends with repentance rather than condemnation, Maegan's journey continues not as a story of defeat, but of hope, forgiveness, and the courage to begin again.

Brian Poe bats for proactive climate action at National Climate Resilience Forum. For FPJ Panday Bayanihan Party-List Rep. Brian Poe, proactive climate action and stronger collaboration among government, civil society, and the youth are key to Philippine climate resilience. This was the main take away from his message Wednesday, July 23 as he addressed participants at the National Climate Resilience Forum 2026. Representing the House of Representatives and serving as a member of the House Committee on Climate Change, Poe joined Climate Change Commission officials, National Youth Commission Chairperson Undersecretary Jeff Ortega, fellow members of the House, local government officials, youth leaders, and development partners in advancing the country's climate resilience agenda. Poe began by expressing his gratitude to the Climate Change Commission (CCC) for organizing the forum and bringing together key stakeholders to strengthen the country's climate resilience efforts. Congratulating the Commission for convening the gathering, Poe emphasized that the forum's theme reflects a crucial shift in the country's approach to climate action. "Resilience is not just about responding to disasters. It is about actually preparing our nation before disasters strike," Poe said. He noted that building resilience requires long-term planning, science-based policymaking, and investments that enable communities to withstand the growing impacts of climate change before emergencies occur. Drawing from his recent participation at the 11th Our Ocean Conference in Kenya, where he delivered the Philippine National Statement, Poe highlighted the importance of translating global climate commitments into concrete local action. "While climate change is a global challenge, resilience is ultimately built at home—in our communities, in our cities and municipalities, and through the decisions we make as a nation," he said. Poe explained that Filipinos experience the impacts of climate change firsthand through stronger storms, threats to food security, and the challenges faced by vulnerable communities, making climate resilience an urgent national priority. The Pangasinan-based solon also stressed that conferences such as the National Climate Resilience Forum are essential because they bring together government agencies, legislators, the private sector, non-government organizations, and the youth to develop policies that are proactive rather than reactive. Congress' contribution As a legislator, Poe said Congress must create the conditions for local government units (LGUs) to access climate financing, harness innovation, and make science-based decisions. He likewise highlighted several climate initiatives currently being advanced in the House of Representatives, including measures on carbon credits, the blue economy, and the green circular economy. Poe also called for continued support for the country's 30x30 conservation goal, for which he is the principal author of a House resolution supporting the protection of 30 percent of the Philippines' land and marine ecosystems for future generations. Sharing encouraging developments from the international stage, Poe noted that during the Our Ocean Conference, the Philippines stood out by reporting that it had already exceeded one of its commitments under the Great Blue Wall Initiative. Instead of merely announcing future targets, the country reported that it has already established 64 marine protected area networks, surpassing its commitment of 60 by 2028. "This demonstrates that the Philippines is emerging as a global leader in sustainability and marine conservation," Poe said. Poe assured stakeholders that Congress remains committed to advancing climate-responsive legislation and emphasized that lasting resilience can only be achieved through a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach.

Flood triggered by ‘habagat’ inundates Davao City. DAVAO CITY – Heavy rain in the mountainous parts of this city spawned massive flooding in riverside communities in Tugbok and Talomo Districts here on Friday night, July 24. The massive flooding reportedly trapped dozens of families in their houses while some were forced to climb to the roof of their houses. Many residents turned to social media to ask for rescue as floodwaters rose in their areas. At 5 p.m. July 24, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) issued a moderate to heavy rainfall advisory in many parts of Mindanao, including Davao del Sur and this city due to the southwest monsoon or habagat. At 6:38 p.m., the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO) placed the Talomo River under “Code Red” or critical level due to continuous rise in water level. The CDRMMO ordered a mandatory evacuation for residents living on the banks of Talomo River in Barangay Talomo Proper. Shortly before 9 p.m., floodwaters swamped portions of Central Park village in Bangkal, Barangay Talomo. A few hours later, people living near the Talomo River posted on social media that flood waters was above human height. In Tugbok District, flood water inundated residential areas and the highway at around 7 p.m. Residential areas on the Talomo River were swamped with flood water, prompting residents to seek refuge on their rooftops. By 9 p.m., responders from different agencies and volunteer groups were mobilized to rescue trapped residents in Talomo and Tugbok Districts. Rescue operations continued until dawn Saturday. The city government has yet to release the number of affected families as verifications are still ongoing. But a report from the Philippine Coast Guard District-Southeastern Mindanao showed that 72 families or 301 individuals were temporarily sheltered at the Lourdes Evacuation Center in Matina Aplaya. The Talomo River headwater is located in the foothills of Mount Talomo in Baguio District. The river cuts passes through mountainous areas of this city and residential areas before draining into the Davao Gulf. Six areas from Tugbok District to Talomo District were flooded on Friday evening. Floodwater started to recede at dawn Saturday.

PH women's lacrosse team makes worlds debut but yields to Israel. The Philippine women’s lacrosse team made a historic debut but yielded a 12-6 loss to Israel in the opener of the 2026 World Lacrosse Women's Championship at the Oi Hockey Stadium in Tokyo, Japan Friday, July 24. The Nationals put up a gallant fight in the first two frames, trailing by just two points before heading into the break. However, the momentum shifted as the Israelis rolled over the Filipina bets off a rousing second-half performance. Kalena Johnson, who scored the country’s first-ever goal in the meet, starred in the contest after earning Player of the Match honor. The next two games are crucial for the Philippines to secure a quarterfinal berth. It battles host Japan, which notched a rousing 21-5 win over Czech Republic, this Sunday, July 26, at the same venue. Bracketed in Pool D, the Nationals could drop to the classification round if they finish at third or fourth place of the said group. Last year, the Philippines women’s crew punched its ticket to the worlds after winning a bronze medal in the Asia-Pacific Lacrosse Championship in Queensland, Australia. Their continuous participation is part of their bid of earning a coveted spot in 2028 Los Angeles Olympics where women’s lacrosse sixes was recently included.

'Walang mga ebidensiya': Pia Cayetano throws shade at Chel Diokno in Facebook video. Senator Pia Cayetano appeared to take a swipe at House prosecutor and Akbayan Party-list Rep. Chel Diokno in a Facebook video wherein she criticized the latter's responses during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. The video, which was uploaded directly to Pia Cayetano's official Facebook page rather than shared from another account on Friday, July 24, carried the captions "Nagbabakasakali lang" (Just trying his luck) and "Walang mga ebidensiya pero nag-aakusa na" (They're making accusations without any evidence). It featured edited clips of Diokno's exchange with Senator Alan Peter Cayetano. In the impeachment trial, all senators including the Cayetano siblings are acting as senator-judges. A "laughing" sound effect was even added to the end of the video. However, it cut short Diokno's response. Presiding officer Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero has yet to reply on the matter. What happened During the trial, a lengthy exchange unfolded between Alan Cayetano and Diokno over the prosecution's bid to subpoena Duterte's financial records, with the debate centering on whether the request amounted to a "fishing expedition". Cayetano argued that prosecutors should already have sufficient evidence before seeking access to Duterte's bank, Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR), and Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA)-related records covering nearly two decades. He repeatedly pressed Diokno on whether the prosecution had proof of unexplained wealth or was merely searching through financial documents in hopes of uncovering incriminating evidence. The senator also questioned why prosecutors were asking the Senate to compel the production of records they had yet to obtain, emphasizing the distinction between "ultimate facts" and "evidentiary facts". He further raised what he described as an inconsistency in the House's approach, noting that lawmakers did not pursue President Marcos' bank records when an impeachment complaint was previously filed against him. 'Chill' Diokno The exchange quickly gained traction online, with many social media users commending Diokno for maintaining his composure throughout the questioning by both Alan Peter and Pia Cayetano. All three are lawyers. Clips of the proceedings circulated widely, earning the House prosecutor the nickname "Chill Diokno" for his calm responses despite persistent questioning. Responding to the accusations, Diokno rejected the characterization of the subpoena request as a "fishing expedition." He said such an expedition occurs only when investigators seek records on the mere "off chance" of discovering evidence. According to the rookie cong7, the prosecution's request was narrowly tailored and supported by findings from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), which allegedly identified P6.7 billion in financial transactions that appeared inconsistent with Duterte's declared net worth. He maintained that the prosecution was only seeking documents necessary to establish the complete "evidentiary facts." Diokno also defended the House's decision to transmit the impeachment complaint without first presenting all supporting evidence, saying the Constitution envisions the Senate—not the House—as the body that conducts the actual trial. Requiring the House to complete the entire evidentiary process beforehand, he argued, would undermine that constitutional framework. Addressing Cayetano's comparison with the impeachment complaint against President Marcos, Diokno said the two cases were fundamentally different. He explained that the complaint against Marcos had been dismissed at the House level because it failed to allege the required "ultimate facts" needed to establish an impeachable offense. He added that the Senate impeachment court is not tasked with reviewing how the House disposed of previous impeachment complaints. Stonehill case Pia Cayetano brought up 1967 Supreme Court ruling in Stonehill v. Diokno, and asked whether the prosecution's request for Duterte's decades-old financial and tax records resembled the broad "general warrants" struck down in that landmark case. The decision involved then-Justice Secretary Jose W. "Ka Pepe" Diokno, the father of House prosecutor Chel Diokno. In response, Chel distinguished the two situations, explaining that Stonehill v. Diokno dealt with search warrants that authorize law enforcement to enter premises and seize property, making them inherently more intrusive. By contrast, he said the prosecution was asking the court to issue a subpoena duces tecum, which simply directs a person or institution to produce specific, relevant, and identifiable documents for use in the proceedings.

Trump delivers insult-filled speech at correspondents' dinner. President Donald Trump returned to the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association dinner Friday night, delivering a rambling, hour-long speech that praised some journalists, took potshots at others, made jokes about public figures' weight and intellect, and quipped about a third presidential term. He assured the crowd of journalists, though, that he'd scrapped the most biting parts of his remarks. “That was going to be a doozy,” Trump said about the speech he’d been prepared to give in April, before a gunman upended the original dinner and forced its postponement. “As I said three months ago, the show must go on,” the president said to begin his remarks, hailing the decision to reschedule the dinner. He referred to “the attempted mass murder” that could have happened that night in April, but then moved largely to humor – and insults. Trump's return to the correspondents' dinner – and his promise to come back next year as well – represented a notable moment in his relationship with the news media, which he has attacked, sued, and taken administrative action against since he began his second term early last year. Among the audience members were reporters he had denounced and barred from events. Trump’s sometimes off-color speech, which lasted just over an hour, was full of vague potshots directed at individuals he doesn’t like – from Jane Fonda to Bruce Springsteen to “Barack Hussein Obama.” The audience, reacting at first with some friendly laughs, slowly quieted to scattered titters as the insults piled up. Among other targets of Trump’s humor: Late-night hosts Jimmy Fallon and Jimmy Kimmel; Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn.; California Gov. Gavin Newsom; former New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie, and Trump's own speechwriters, whose jokes he sometimes criticized even as he delivered them. Some of the comments flirted with racism. The president also spent some time expressing pride in the ballroom at the Waldorf Astoria hotel, formerly the Trump International Hotel. “It’s great to be back at a place that I know very well, because I built it,” Trump said. He also made reference to the journalism awards that had been handed out earlier in the evening, most of them for stories challenging him and his administration. “Do I have a say in those awards?” he asked with a grimace. He made a brief mention of the Iran war and several remarks about the ballroom he is building at the White House. He also used the occasion to joke about the possibility he would serve a third term – something barred by the US Constitution's 22nd Amendment. “Just like my presidency, the second time is always better,” the president quipped. “And the third time will be better yet.” He added: “I’m only kidding.” Then, at the end, he donned a red cap that said “Trump 2028” and delivered the “scoop” that he was running again. Earlier, Trump had entered the ballroom to polite applause, and was thanked for his support by outgoing White House Correspondents’ Association president Weijia Jiang of CBS News. After dinner, he then sat through more than an hour of awards presentations. One of the winners, Tyler Pager of the New York Times, was in fact one of the reporters who had been subpoenaed by Trump’s Justice Department over his reporting about Trump’s Qatari-gifted Air Force One jet. Those subpoenas were withdrawn on Thursday in a New York courtroom – just one of the arenas where the president, in his second term, has been seeking to control media coverage that displeases him. The rescheduled dinner was taking place at a smaller venue this time that held only about 700 people. Security was markedly tighter. Guests entered via a single entrance, through two ID checks and past a detection dog, armed officers, and security guards. There was no red carpet and no separate cocktail receptions preceding the dinner. “Let’s try this again,” Jiang quipped, welcoming the crowd. The White House press corps, she noted, “always have a follow-up.” Turning serious, she referred back to the trauma and confusion of the original dinner in April. “Tonight, our message is this: We are back,” she said. “We will not be intimidated. We refuse to let an act of violence have the final word.” Early in his speech, Trump signaled that he had decided to tone it down. But he kept some zingers. Like this one, to the media-heavy audience: “This is really the largest group of ‘Trump Derangement Syndrome’ people put together at one time.” Besides the pared-down approach, there was another change at Friday’s dinner: Two additional awards. One was presented to Victor Gonzales, the Secret Service agent who was staffing a security checkpoint in April and was struck in his protective vest. Gonzales “placed himself directly in harm’s way and engaged the armed suspect,” Jiang said. “He stayed in the fight and the attacker was stopped.” A second award was presented to the staff of the Washington Hilton hotel, site of the first dinner, hailed for professionalism under pressure. The dress code this time was a looser “black tie optional,” and dinner included grilled peach and burrata salad, lobster, and beef Wellington. The evening, as in April, featured entertainment by mentalist Oz Pearlman – who this time got the chance to do his act. Jiang and her fellow board members had worked hard to bring about this WHCA dinner 2.0, not wanting to let a violent act – or the image of colleagues hiding under tables – remain the final thought. Announcing the rescheduling, she emphasized the dinner’s stated purpose: “A celebration of a free press and the vital role of journalism in our democracy for over a century.” But it’s also clear that some people felt the dinner should not be rescheduled at all. Many never thought it was much of a good look in the first place, with the sight of journalists in formal wear cozying up to their sources, or the objects of their reporting. “It undermines the public faith in how the press does its work, and it makes it look like we are pals with the people we cover,” Kelly McBride, an ethics expert at the Poynter Institute, a journalism think tank, said when the deliberations were taking place. The new dinner came at a time of fast-increasing tension between the media and a president who, in his second term, has tried to exert pressure on media outlets he is unhappy with in a variety of ways. That pressure has ranged from sanctions against members of the White House press corps to regulatory actions through the Federal Communications Commission to outright lawsuits. Those tensions have only escalated since April. Trump, though, ended with an attempt to mend fences 00 to a point. “I have a lot of respect for your profession,” he told the assembled journalists. He also touted his own success, and declared: “When I'm not around, you're all gonna be broke.” And he concluded about the evening: “I didn't know what to expect. It's far worse than I originally thought.” (AP)

Unbeaten SMB, NLEX dispute Group A lead. It’s a battle between two undefeated teams — one looking to prove its hot start is no fluke, the other aiming to assert its status as one of the teams to beat – as the clash between NLEX and San Miguel highlight a blockbuster double-header at the Smart Araneta Coliseum on Sunday, July 26. Both protecting a 3-0 slate, fireworks are expected as the Road Warriors and the Beermen dispute the top spot of the Group A standings, while Barangay Ginebra and Rain or Shine figure in a rematch of the last conference’s semifinals in the second game at 7:30 p.m. More than trying to keep their record pristine, NLEX head coach Jimmy Alapag is excited about facing the perennial contender in San Miguel, seeing it as a great opportunity to test the mettle of his squad. “He’s (June Mar Fajardo) dominated this league for years. So I think it will be a great test for us. Not just for our big guys, but I think for our entire team. I think San Miguel has stamped its legacy in this league with their dominance behind June Mar,” said Alapag. The Road Warriors are coming into the contest off a two-week respite and that should help them get more accustomed to the system under Alapag who only took over the team during the short offseason. But NLEX isn’t facing a typical San Miguel team which have leaned and depended on Fajardo alone. For one, CJ Perez and import George King have shown great chemistry with the rest of the Beermen, evident with the pair of explosive performances in their 128-122 win over Converge. Meanwhile in the second game, it will be an interesting rematch between Ginebra and Rain or Shine, which after dropping their first few games, finally barged into the winning column. Now, the two teams are aiming for a huge followup. "Medyo malapit na kaming maging desperado at kailangan manalo. Doon sa previous games, talo kami sa rebounding and we gave up a high-percentage shooting. We made it a point na pagsikapan na makadepensa at maka-rebound kami," said ROS head coach Guiao.

Don't miss ‘Héritage’ at Flame. Flame at Discovery Primea is one of those restaurants that always warrants a return visit. Beyond its polished dining room, the restaurant offers some of the finest views in Makati. Look out through its floor-to-ceiling windows, or step onto the adjoining alfresco lounge for a breath of fresh air, and you're rewarded with a panorama that stretches from the tree-lined streets of Urdaneta Village to the ever-changing Makati skyline. Then there's the food. Flame has long impressed me with cooking that is confident without being showy. Every plate is thoughtfully composed, driven by sound technique rather than unnecessary flourishes, allowing quality ingredients to speak for themselves. It was the perfect stage for “Héritage,” the latest installment of Discovery Primea's “Elements of Flavor” series, a one-night-only dinner on July 28 that reunites executive chef Luis Chikiamco with one of his earliest mentors, chef Cyrille Soenen, technical director of Le Cordon Bleu Ateneo de Manila and a Maître Cuisinier de France. Joining them are fellow Le Cordon Bleu Ateneo faculty members chef Julien Bispo, pastry chef, and chef Régis Doré, master baker, bringing together decades of experience spanning Michelin-starred restaurants, luxury hotels, international competitions, and culinary education. For Luis, the evening carries personal significance. "Cooking with chef Cyrille again feels like coming full circle. I learned so much from him early in my career, and having him here at Flame makes this collaboration especially meaningful. Héritage reflects the values we've always shared, respect for technique, appreciation for great ingredients, and the belief that the best meals are the ones that bring people together," he said during the preview dinner last July 21. That philosophy became evident from the first course and continued throughout the evening. While the menu spans dishes such as Pulutan à la Prince Albert, Lobster Salad Remoulade, Crispy Korean Chicken "Oyster," Halibut Viennoise, Kurobuta Pork Sando, Pigeon Tourte, Trio Sorbet, Chocolate Tiramisu Tart, and Petit Fours, what stood out is the discipline behind every plate. Among the dishes, the Halibut Viennoise was my clear favorite. It demonstrated the techniques that define truly accomplished cooking—technically precise, elegantly balanced, and allowing the fish to remain the centerpiece. I savored every bite. The Pigeon Tourte was equally memorable, while dessert, particularly the Chocolate Tiramisu Tart, provided a refined ending. For Cyrille, the evening was never about revisiting old recipes. "To me, heritage is much more than preserving recipes. It is about preserving techniques, craftsmanship, respect for the ingredients, and honoring the chefs who came before us. We don't simply recreate dishes from the past, we seek to understand the methods behind them and carry them forward while creating something meaningful for today's guests." Working alongside Luis again, he said, felt effortless because they continue to share the same philosophy. "Working with chef Luis again has been a real pleasure. We created many memorable dinners together over the years, and seeing him now lead the culinary team at Discovery Primea makes me very proud. Developing this menu was easy because we share the same philosophy, we challenge ourselves every day while always thinking about the pleasure we can bring to our guests. I sincerely hope this is only the first of many collaborations." For diners, however, there is only one opportunity to experience this one. Héritage will be served for one night only on July 28, with dinner seatings at 6:30 p.m., 7 p.m., and 8 p.m. Reservations are required. If Flame already deserves a place on your dining list for its food and one of Makati's finest views, this collaboration offers one more compelling reason to return before it disappears.

Georgia's Okefenokee Swamp among new additions to join UNESCO's Worls Heritage List. SEOUL, South Korea (AP) – The Okefenokee Swamp in Georgia, a centuries-old porcelain center in eastern China, and tidal flats in western South Korea were among several sites added to the World Heritage List on Saturday in a UN committee meeting in South Korea. The UNESCO meetings in Busan, which continue through next Wednesday, are reviewing dozens of other nominations, including the D-Day landing beaches in France, Mount Olympus in Greece, and the ancient Japanese capitals of Asuka and Fujiwara. The Okefenokee Swamp is regarded as one of the world’s largest freshwater ecosystems, encompassing a vast network of wetlands that supports exceptional biodiversity and serves as the source of two major rivers. Its largely undisturbed peat beds preserve a 5,000-year record of environmental change, making the swamp both a globally significant natural habitat and a valuable source of information on long-term environmental change, according to a UNESCO description. While the World Heritage designation places the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge alongside iconic US landmarks such as the Grand Canyon, some locals have opposed the listing, fearing it would increase UN involvement in managing the site. “We accept this inscription not as a finish line, but as a commitment to keep the Okefenokee wild, resilient, and thriving for generations to come,” said Kim Bednarek, executive director of the non-profit Okefenokee Swamp Park that’s worked with the US government on the refuge’s nomination package. The committee also decided to expand the World Heritage listing of the South Korean “getbol” tidal flats with four additional coastal wetlands in Seosan, Goheung, Muan, and Yeosu in the country’s west. UNESCO had previously inscribed four other South Korean tidal flats in 2021 for their biodiversity and crucial role as a stopover for migratory birds. South Korea’s Foreign Ministry said the expanded designation of the tidal flats “reaffirms the importance of international cooperation for the conservation of the Yellow Sea ecosystem and the East Asian-Australasian Flyway,” a major migratory bird route that stretches from the Arctic through Asia to Australia and New Zealand. Another new addition to the World Heritage List was the handicraft porcelain industry sites in China’s Jingdezhen. The sites trace the evolution of handcrafted porcelain production in China from the 10th to the 19th centuries, showcasing innovations that helped make Jingdezhen a leading center for fine porcelain, with its blue-and-white porcelain becoming a global symbol of Chinese craftsmanship, according to UNESCO.

4,000 cops secure SONA in Western Visayas. ILOILO CITY – Almost 4,000 police officers were deployed in Western Visayas to secure the 2026 State-of- the-Nation Address (SONA) of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Monday, July 27. The Police Regional Office-6 has intensified security measures for Aklan, Antique, Capiz, Guimaras, and Iloilo provinces as well as the capital city of Iloilo. “We are fully prepared to ensure that the public remains safe and that activities across the region remain peaceful,” said PRO-6 Director Police Brig. Gen. Randulf Tuaño. Other law enforcement agencies are supporting the police and activists were reminded of the “No Permit, No Rally” policy of the Philippine National Police (PNP). Police Major Lailyn Sencil, PRO-6 chief information officer, reiterated that they respect the right to freedom of expression and stressed that protest actions must be lawful and peaceful.

San Fernando hopes Singapore domestic worker case won't ruin OFWs' good reputation. Kamanggagawa Party-list Rep. Eli San Fernando expressed hope that one act of wrongdoing in Singapore won't tarnish the good name of overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) all over the world. San Fernando was reacting to the case of domestic worker Raguindin Bassig, who, upon deeper reflection, made him lament the difficulties that Filipino workers face each day. "We respect the judicial process and legal proceedings of Singapore, and wrongdoing must certainly be matched with corresponding penalties," San Fernando said over the weekend. "This incident, however, brings to light the deep systemic realities that continue to push millions of Filipinos to seek employment abroad under highly vulnerable conditions," said the House minority bloc member. Bassig, 47, an OFW in Singapore, was sentenced to three years and two months in jail earlier this month after pleading guilty to two counts of theft by a servant. It was reported that, in a period of over four years, she took US$168,000 worth of cash and jewellery from her employer. Bassig allegedly used the loot to buy condominium units, cars, and land back home in the Philippines. "Every year, thousands of our workers, predominantly women, leave their families to take on demanding, live-in domestic roles overseas, often working under intense isolation, long hours, and severe socioeconomic pressure," San Fernando noted. "We must not sensationalize and allow singular cases of wrongdoing to overshadow or detract from the honest, dignified, and indispensable labor provided by the vast majority of our [OFWs], who keep both foreign households and our national economy afloat," he stressed. The neophyte congressman said the case serves as a stark reminder of "why we must aggressively pursue genuine economic development and dignified, living wage jobs here at home". "Our ultimate goal must always be to build a society where working abroad is a voluntary choice, not a desperate necessity forced by poverty," said San Fernando. The pro-worker party-list solon further said: "We remain committed to pushing for stronger labor protections (both bilateral and in compliance with international labor conventions), robust oversight, and comprehensive reintegration programs that safeguard the welfare, dignity, and rights of all Filipino workers, wherever they may be in the world." Data from the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) bared that as of early 2026, there were about 1.8 million OFWs deployed worldwide. However, recent conflicts in the Middle East caused a sharp 45 percent drop in deployments in the first quarter compared to 2025. Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) remain the top destinations, though both saw significant declines.

'Miss Behave' cast hopes series sparks empathy for victims of leaked private photos. The stars of "Miss Behave" hope viewers walk away from the series with one important lesson: never judge someone's life by what they see online.
