During the latest Star Magic Spotlight press conference at the Dolphy Theater in ABS-CBN, Quezon City, the cast shared how the youth drama has resonated with audiences by tackling difficult but increasingly relevant issues, including leaked private photos, online shaming, misogyny, abuse, teenage trauma, and the pressure to fit in. Directed by Ivan Andrew Payawal, "Miss Behave" follows five high school girls whose lives are turned upside down after their private photos are leaked online. As they become the targets of gossip, judgment, and humiliation, they are forced to confront their own fears while seeking justice. For the cast, the series stands out because it isn't afraid to discuss conversations many young people often keep to themselves. "It's also about female rage, revenge, and woman empowerment," Rain Parani said, describing the show's deeper themes. Rans Rafol believes one of the series' strongest messages is a reminder to look beyond the carefully curated world of social media. "Hindi po talaga tayo pwedeng mag-based sa nakikita lang natin sa social media. Hindi natin alam kung anong pinagdadaanan ng mga tao," she said. "Sana mas maging kinder at mas maging maunawain sila sa mga tao. A little kindness goes a long way." The actors also explained how each character represents a different struggle experienced by today's youth. Rain plays Isabel, whose fearless personality hides emotional vulnerabilities. Andi Abaya portrays April, a tech-savvy student dealing with family issues and loneliness. Rans plays Dessalyn, a scholar who creates an alter ego in an effort to fit into an elite science high school. Raven Rigor portrays Ant, whose own secrets threaten to surface. LA Santos plays Migo, a morally complex character whose true intentions remain uncertain. Zach Guerrero appears as Earl, a student desperate to break into the school's popular crowd. Akira Morishita plays Warren, a fiercely loyal friend, while JC Alcantara portrays Cole, the ambitious leader of the Kings of Sosh whose family expectations and personal choices fuel much of the story's conflict. The cast admitted that portraying the emotional aftermath of the leaked images proved to be among the most difficult parts of filming, with many scenes requiring them to explore the fear, shame, and isolation experienced by victims of online abuse. As "Miss Behave" heads into its final two episodes, the actors hope viewers continue following not just the mystery, but also the conversations the series has sparked about empathy, accountability, and the real-life consequences of digital harassment. They also expressed gratitude for the growing online support the show has received, saying fan edits and discussions on social media have helped introduce the series to a wider audience. "Miss Behave" streams exclusively on iWant, with its final two episodes premiering Wednesdays at 8 p.m.

Better than fare hike? LTFRB eyes expansion, increase of fuel discount for PUVs. The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) appears to be leaning towards sustaining and expanding fuel discount instead of fare increase, citing the unstable security situation in the Middle East as the reason. LTFRB chairman Vigor D. Mendoza II said the fuel discount as an alternative to fare hike was proposed in some of its meetings with government agencies and stakeholders, saying the unpredictable situation in the Middle East is making it hard to decide on the appropriate fare hike. It was recalled that air strikes continue despite repeated ceasefire agreements between the United States and Iran. “We are factoring everything in the conduct of review and this includes the fact that it is difficult to do so because the situation in the Middle East remains unpredictable and unstable,” said Mendoza. “Increasing and expanding the fuel discount is the most logical and practical measure in the middle of the uncertainty on the situation in the Middle East. This will be discussed in the ongoing discussions,” he added. Earlier, the LTFRB announced that it would recompute an appropriate fare increase after transport groups sent a letter to President Marcos urging the implementation of the after fare hike that was deferred in March. In March, the LTFRB approved a fare increase but this was set aside by Marcos who said any fare hike is not timely since it was the height of the armed conflict in the Middle East. Amid the discussions, there were proposals that the ongoing fuel discount be expanded and increased instead in order to cover the additional operational costs that the public utility vehicle (PUV) sector has been raising. Currently, the P10 per liter fuel discount covers passenger jeepneys and UV Express, the most common modes of transportation being used by Filipino commuters on their way to workplaces and back to their homes. More than 87,000 PUVs already benefited from the P10 per liter fuel discount and as of latest data, the number of PUVs listed in the system already reached more than 143,000. “We are looking into this proposal as the last option because the discussions on the matter are ongoing, and these discussions include public consultations with stakeholders nationwide,” said Chairman Vigor. While arguments raised by the supporters of fuel discount that it will not hurt the commuters and public because of the concerns on the inflation effects of any fare hike, Chairman Vigor said increasing the fuel discount and expanding it to cover as many PUVs would entail huge budgets.

Celebrities react to viral Rome fight: Is social media glorifying vigilantism?. A punch can go viral in seconds. But a celebrity's reaction? It can make it explode. That's exactly what happened after a video of two supposed Filipinos fighting an alleged pickpocket aboard a train in Rome, Italy spread across social media. It drew praise not only from thousands of netizens but from several celebrities as well. Among those who appeared to show support were Charo Santos , Pokwang , Bretman Rock , Eula Valdez , IC Mendoza and Enzo Pineda , echoing the sentiment shared by many Filipinos online: the alleged thief had it coming. It's easy to understand why the video struck a nerve. The young man seen in the footage wasn't exactly winning sympathy. He allegedly mocked the Filipinos confronting him and even exposed himself while the cameras were rolling. When punches started flying inside the train, plenty of viewers felt they were watching instant karma. The comments reflected that. There were jokes about Manny Pacquiao , remarks about Filipinos not backing down from bullies, and applause for the supposed OFWs who stood their ground. The original video came from YouTuber DJE Media, whose content often involves tracking down alleged pickpockets in Europe. It's a formula that's become increasingly common online: find a suspected criminal, put a camera in their face, wait for something dramatic to happen. Drama sells, more so, if celebrities join in. And once celebrities started sharing their reactions, well, welcome to internet celebrity-hood. But that's where the discussion gets interesting. To be clear: We are not defending pickpocketing. We are not defending the behavior shown by the young man in the video either. But if these confrontations become the kind of content people actively look forward to, are we also normalizing something else? Vigilantism has always made for compelling entertainment. Batman built a franchise on it. So did countless action movies where the hero skips the paperwork and dishes out justice with his fists. But real life isn't a two-hour movie. A person suspected of stealing could be carrying a weapon. Someone trying to play hero could end up seriously hurt. Someone wrongly accused could become the victim instead. None of those possibilities make for viral clips. The Rome video may be remembered as the clip where an alleged pickpocket got what many believed he deserved. Or it may be remembered as another moment when violence became content, and content became entertainment. As Maximus roared before a bloodthirsty Roman crowd in "Gladiator," "Are you not entertained?" Watching the internet's reaction to this fight, perhaps the better question is: Well... are we?

Lacson says Taguig infra project probe could lead to plunder charges. Senator Panfilo "Ping" Lacson said those who may be implicated in the ongoing investigation into allegedly anomalous slope protection and drainage projects in Taguig City could face plunder charges if the evidence establishes a series of unlawful transactions involving at least ₱50 million. In a radio interview on Friday night, Lacson said the investigation has reached a stage where prosecutors may be able to pursue the non-bailable offense, provided the legal requirements are met. "Kung series of acts tapos P50 million (ang involved), walang ibang mapupuntahan kundi plunder (If it is a series of acts involving at least P50 million, there's no other way to go but to file plunder charges)," he said. Lacson said the investigation has gained momentum in recent days, noting that the evidence gathered so far has strengthened the case. A day earlier, he described the probe as having reached the point of "SHOOT SA KALDERO," suggesting that investigators were zeroing in on those responsible. The senator also said his team continued working through the weekend to pursue additional leads and avoid losing momentum in the investigation. In a post on X on Saturday, Lacson said investigators remained focused on bringing the inquiry to its "logical conclusion." "WORKING ON A WEEKEND: today, a Saturday, we haven’t slowed down in following up the leads to maintain the momentum gained since we started investigating the anomalous slope protection and drainage projects in Taguig. Our goal is to reach its logical conclusion," he wrote. The projects under investigation are located in Taguig City, the political bailiwick of Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano. Lacson maintained that the inquiry is not driven by political or personal considerations but by the need to hold accountable anyone found to have participated in wrongdoing. "This is not about friendship or personal fights, this is about accountability. Kung walang accountability bakit ko pipilitin (This is not about friendship or personal fights but about accountability. If there is no accountability, why would I push through with the investigation)?" he said.

Senior walks 20,000 steps daily to feed stray cats in Binondo. Before Manila fully wakes, when the streets are still half-empty and the air is quiet, 70-year-old “Uncle Rooney,” a longtime resident of Binondo, is already walking. Not for exercise. Not to pass the time. But for the stray cats waiting in the shadows of Tutuban, Binondo, and Sta. Cruz. With plastic bags of food in hand, he moves through familiar streets, stopping at corners most people ignore. He calls out softly, and almost on cue, they appear. From under carts, behind parked vans, out of narrow alleyways. Some hesitant, others already certain. They know him. “Pag tinawag ko sila, lumalabas na ’yan (When I call them, they come out),” he said. “Parang alam nila na kakain na (It’s like they already know it’s time to eat).” What started in 2015 as feeding a few cats around Binondo has since grown into a daily ritual he cannot walk away from. He no longer keeps count. On most days, dozens of cats meet him along his route, sometimes more, depending on where he passes. The numbers changed over time, but the responsibility stayed. So did the routine. Now retired after 37 years of running an electronics repair shop, Uncle Rooney has built his days around these walks. He lives alone, something he says allowed him to fully commit to the routine that now fills his time. He walks between 20,000 steps daily, even as his knees weaken and his hearing fades. “At my age, mahina na tuhod ko… pero blessing pa rin na kaya ko pang maglakad. Kahit papaano, may nagagawa pa ako para sa iba ( At my age, my knees are already weak… but it’s still a blessing that I can walk. At least in some way, I can still do something for others) .” What used to be movement has become meaning. “If I don’t feed them, my day is not complete,” he said. “Parang may kulang talaga (It really feels like something is missing).” The routine comes at a cost. On most days, he spends around P2,000 to P3,000 on cat food, sometimes more when there are new strays or kittens along his route. Some cats prefer fish, others dry food, so he adjusts depending on what they will eat. There are days when donations come in, especially after his story began circulating online. But support is inconsistent, and much of the expense still comes from his own savings. Uncle Rooney has no social media accounts and no digital footprint. The only phone he carries is an old keypad Nokia, no apps, no notifications, just something for calls, including those from people who want to help. When he encounters injured cats, those hit by vehicles or left weak on the roadside, he brings them to clinics, sometimes spending P6,000 to P8,000 just to give them a chance to survive. Before this, he once tried feeding homeless children, but stopped after becoming discouraged. Some would reject the food or waste it, he said, and the experience left him disheartened. It was later, in Binondo, that he started feeding stray cats, and never really stopped. Now, every stop along his route feels familiar. There are cats he recognizes, some he even considers favorites. When he arrives, they come out, almost as if they have been waiting. Even rain does not stop him. He simply puts on a raincoat and continues. There is no audience when he starts his walk, no recognition waiting at the end of it. Just the same streets, the same corners, and the same quiet expectation. And every morning, without fail, he shows up. Because somewhere along his route, in dim alleyways and under parked trucks, something is waiting for him to come back.

DND seeks recruitment of more digital technology experts for PH military. The Department of National Defense (DND) is eyeing the recruitment of more professionals with an intense background on artificial intelligence, cyber operations and other emerging technologies which it said are essential to modernizing and expanding the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP). DND Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro, Jr. said the AFP was already directed to pursue such blueprint under the move to expand the Direct Commission Program in the military that covers recruitment and commissioning of qualified Advance Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC) graduates, deserving enlisted personnel, and highly skilled professionals. By highly skilled professionals, Teodoro is referring to cyber operations, artificial intelligence, engineering, aviation, communications, and research and development “to develop a more agile, technologically capable, and multidisciplinary military force.” “The expanded Direct Commission Program supports the AFP’s modernization efforts and the Comprehensive Archipelagic Defense Concept by ensuring the Armed Forces can attract, develop, and retain the specialized talent needed to address evolving defense and security challenges, and safeguard national security,” the DND said in a statement released on Saturday, July 25. In the same statement, it said Teodoro also instructed the AFP to establish merit-based pathways for commissioning outstanding enlisted personnel. The AFP was also tasked to consider reasonable accommodations for qualified persons with disabilities whose expertise are vital to defense missions, and develop appropriate training and career development programs for personnel recruited through these non-traditional entry pathways. “By strengthening the AFP’s human capital, the DND continues to build the capabilities required to defend the nation, sustain internal security gains, and address emerging threats in an increasingly complex strategic environment,” the DND said in a statement released on Saturday, July 25. The DND said all implementing guidelines must remain consistent with existing laws and uphold the AFP’s professional, operational, and security standards.

Yeo, Tiu shine as Xavier draws first blood against Yap-led Hua Siong in FCAAI Finals. Joseph Yeo and Chris Tiu reprised their legendary partnership decades ago and Xavier School outlasted the James Yap-led Hua Siong College-Iloilo, 75-72, in Game 1of the 40-years division 40-years division finals in the Fil-Chinese Athletic Association Inc. (FCAAI) on Friday, July 24, at the FilOil EcoOil Centre in San Juan. Though the icons of the Powersox-AcroCity-backed Xavier were no longer as speedy and quick as before, Yeo and Tiu remained sharp and deadly from afar as they made the clutch plays to beat the reigning champions in the opener of their best-of-three title series before a good-size of spectators. The Golden Stallions can clinch the title and avenge their defeat last year with another win on Monday. Of the two, it was Yeo who struck hardest, scattering 30 points spiked by four triples to beat out Yap in their fiery shootout. Yeo actually scored the team’s last seven points, including a triple that gave them a 71-66 lead. Yap buried two booming triples en route to finishing with 18 points but his efforts were not enough as the Lamtex Pipes-backed Hua Siong suffered their first defeat after completing an 8-game sweep of the elims. Hua Siong also scored an easy 108-74 win over GT Radial-Grace Christian College in the semis. Good thing for Xavier, Tiu also delivered significant numbers with 17 points and accounted for two of the team’s 13 triples against 9 for Hua Siong. Meantime, GCC, drawing 20 points from Allan Anson Tan, finished third in the 9-team field with 60-40 drubbing of SCAG-St. Stephen’s. With Yap struggling, Ken Bono tried to breathe life into their cause but Xavier was not to be denied this time. The league has the backing of Smart Sports, Tanduay Athletics, Genius Hardware, Ultraforce Tires, Cellboy, PGFlex Linoleum, Boysen, Lamtex Pipes, Jiang Nan, Hangry Pares, Powerhouse Tools, L.F. Fireworks, BYD Valenzuela, BAIC, Jetour, Yong Kee Roasting House, 1118 Autospa, and TCL.

Ombudsman files 14 graft charges vs party-list solon over alleged interest in P214 M DPWH contracts. The Office of the Ombudsman (OMB) has charged Uswag Ilonggo Party-list Rep. James “Jojo” Ang Jr. with 14 counts of graft before the Sandiganbayan for allegedly retaining an interest in a construction firm that secured P214 million in Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) contracts while he was in Congress. “While sitting in Congress, Rep. Ang holds a stake in a construction firm that won ₱214 million in DPWH contracts — and was paid nearly ₱199 million for them,” Assistant Ombudsman Jose Dominic “Mico” Clavano IV told reporters covering OMB on Saturday, July 25. According to the OMB, the Constitution bars members of Congress from holding any financial interest in government contracts while serving their terms. “Conflict of interest is not a gray area. It does not require proof that a deal was rigged or that cash changed hands — only that a public official profited, or stood to profit, from a government contract while in office,” said Clavano. “Here, and in many cases, the clear and thick constitutional line is constantly and blatantly being crossed,” he went on. On July 18, the Ombudsman announced that the complaints against Ang and other congressmen have moved to the preliminary investigation stage. Ombudsman Jesus Crispin “Boying” Remulla said the complaints are part of the office’s continuing investigation into alleged conflicts of interest involving lawmakers who are also allegedly contractors. Earlier, the Ombudsman told politicians to choose between public service and private business, saying elected officials should stop engaging in government contracting as the office continues its conflict-of-interest investigations. Remulla said the practice of mixing public office with private business interests must come to an end. Those who wish to pursue business, he said, should stay out of politics.

ASF strikes 2 hog raisers in Bacolod. BACOLOD CITY – The City Veterinary Office (CVO) confirmed on Friday, July 24, that African Swine Fever (ASF) hit two hog raisers in Barangays Granada and Bata in this highly-urbanized city. Two samples were collected in Barangay Bata and both tested positive in the initial and confirmatory laboratory tests, according to the CVO. Four barangays here have recorded confirmed ASF cases – Alijis, Taculing, Granada, and Bata. The CVO has been conducting disinfection activities in identified Ground Zeros or backyard swine areas where ASF-positive animals were housed. These include sanitation and biosecurity procedures to help eliminate potential sources of contamination and protect the local swine population. The disinfection operation is part of the office's immediate containment and control measures aimed at reducing the risk of further virus transmission within the affected area and neighboring communities. The CVO urged all hog raisers in the affected barangays to heighten their biosecurity measures and immediately report any unusual illness or mortality among swine. They also sought the cooperation of farmers, barangay officials, and stakeholders in preventing the further spread of ASF, stressing that cooperation is vital in safeguarding the local swine industry. “By remaining vigilant and adhering to established biosecurity protocols, we can collectively minimize the impact of ASF, protect the livelihoods of our hog raisers, and ensure the continued stability and sustainability of the city’s livestock sector,” the CVO said in a statement. The city’s ASF Task Force has been reactivated to strengthen vigilance against the disease, and the city has prohibited the entry of all live pigs, pork, pork products, from areas with confirmed ASF cases.

Cagayan folk flee Kiyapo. TUGUEGARAO CITY – Authorities evacuated hundreds of residents in this province due to typhoon Kiyapo. The Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (PDRRMO) reported that 258 individuals from 57 families from Allacapan, Buguey, Santa Teresita, Camalanuigan, and Gonzaga were affected by the weather disturbance as of July 24. Two-hundred forty-three individuals from 54 families were temporarily relocated to seven evacuation centers while 15 individuals from three families sought shelter with relatives. The PDRRMO said preemptive evacuation was conducted as a safety measure from flood and landslides. No casualties or storm-related incidents have been recorded as of posting time. The Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (PDRRMC), together with the Task Force Lingkod Cagayan-Quick Response Team (TFLC-QRT), is coordinating with municipal disaster offices for possible emergency response. TFLC stations in Gonzaga, Lal-lo, Ballesteros, and Sanchez Mira are under red alert status to ensure immediate deployment if needed. People were urged to stay alert, follow local government advisories, and remain prepared as Kiyapo continues to affect parts of the province.

Just tell Pinoys the truth: Barbers hits Cayetanos' spliced video on impeachment trial. House impeachment adviser and prosecution panel spokesperson Robert Ace Barbers took issue on Saturday, July 25 with the Cayetano senator-siblings' alleged spliced video about Vice President Sara Duterte's Senate impeachment trial. “We would also like to ask Senator-judge Pia Cayetano and Senator-judge Alan Cayetano to simply tell the Filipino people, especially those that have seen this spliced video, kung ano yung katotohanan (to tell them the truth)," Barbers said. “Dahil nandoon po naman sila nung araw na 'yun, noong habang nagkakaroon ng oral arguments. Alam po nila at dinig na dinig nila kung ano 'yung katotohanan na taliwas o hindi kapareha ng video na kumakalat sa ngayon,” he noted. (Because they were present that day, during the oral arguments. They knew and clearly heard the truth, which is different from what the circulating video shows.) Barbers made these statements in response to the Facebook reels posted by Senator Pia Cayetano, which feature edited portions of the impeachment proceedings. This included exchanges involving Senator Alan Peter Cayetano and House prosecutor Akbayan Party-list Rep. Chel Diokno . “We respect every member of the Senate 8mpeachment court, including Senator Judge Pia Cayetano, and we recognize that everyone is entitled to express their own views, lalo na na dito sa mainit na usapin ng impeachment," Barbers said. “However, we also hope that discussions regarding the impeachment proceedings are presented in a manner that gives the Filipino people the complete and accurate context.” Last week, Diokno, a rookie congressman but an experienced litigator, took on the task of speaking in the oral arguments for the grant of the prosecution panel's subpoena request for respondent Duterte's bank and tax records, as well as Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) reports. Presiding officer Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero ended up granting the prosecution’s request, despite the repeated insistence of the defense lawyers that the pursuit of the financial records was a "fishing expedition". Barbers appealed to the Cayetanos to clarify what really transpired during the oral arguments. "I do hope in the spirit of fairness that the senator-judge showing their impartiality, sana mabago at ma-correct po itong videong ito," said the former overall chairman of the House quad-committee (quad-comm). (I do hope, in the spirit of fairness and with senator-judges showing their impartiality, that this video can be corrected.) Don't rely on social media clips As for the Filipino public that consume such videos regularly, Barbers reiterated his advice. “Ang impeachment trial ay hindi dapat husgahan batay sa ilang segundo ng video o sa mga putol-putol na bahagi nito. Mas mahalaga na makita ng buong publiko kung ano ang kabuuan ng proceedings upang sila mismo makabuo ng kanilang opinion at patas at tamang pang-unawa dito sa mga videos na ito," he said. (The impeachment trial should not be judged based on a few seconds of video or fragmented clips. It is more important for the public to see the entirety of the proceedings so they can form their own opinion and gain fair and proper understanding of these videos.) He said all public officials share the responsibility of protecting public confidence in democratic institutions. “As public officials, we all share the responsibility of strengthening, not weakening public confidence in our institutions. The best way to achieve that is to encourage the public to watch the proceedings in their entirety rather than rely solely on excerpts," Barbers said. “Kaya nga pinapanawagan namin sa ating mga kababayan na subaybayan po itong impeachment trial na ito dahil dito po natin maiiwasan ang pagkalat ng fake news ," he added. (That is why we are calling on our fellow citizens to closely follow this impeachment trial, because this is how we can prevent the spread of fake news.) The ex-Surigao del Norte congressman and governor emphasized that the impeachment proceedings transcend any individual participant. “This proceedings is bigger than any individual. It is about preserving the integrity of the impeachment process and ensuring that the Filipino people receive a fair, complete and truthful picture of what transpired in the court," Barbers said. “So kailangan tayo ang magbuo ng ating opinion. Huwag lamang po natin tingnan kung ano 'yung nakikita natin sa social media at mahalaga na sa ating pagsubaybay dito maiiwasan natin 'yung pagkalat ng maraming, maraming fake news kagaya ng nangyayaring ito na kung saan ay nakikita natin na spliced o hindi kaya ay minanipula yung video na ipinakita," he further said. (So we must form our own opinion. We should not rely only on what we see on social media, and by monitoring the trial we can avoid the spread of much fake news, such as these spliced or manipulated videos being circulated.)

Top ASEAN police officials discuss school shooting after Tacloban gun attack. Top officials of the Philippine National Police (PNP) and their counterparts in Southeast Asia have discussed preventive measures against mass school shootings following the incident in Tacloban City early this month that left three students dead and 20 others wounded. And one of that measures, according to PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr., is to simulate the legislative agenda of Australia where it banned social media access to minors under 16 years old and imposing penalties on social media companies in case of any violation. In the case of the Tacloban school shooting, the shooters were 14-year old and 15-year old and the youngest of them was reported to have been addicted to Gorebox, an online game which Philippine authorities described as known for its graphic depiction of violence. “The Tacloban school shooting was perpetrated by minors and they are CICL (Children in Conflict of the Law). Upon coordination and talk, meetings with our neighboring countries and dialogue partners, they have laws, best practices that we will try to consider,’ said Nartatez. “If other nations are looking at the law in Australia, we can adopt it or improve,” he stressed. The Tacloban school shooting was the first mass shooting in the Philippines, according to Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla. And following that incident that rocked the country’s neighbors in Southeast Asia, Nartatez said it was discussed during the discussion among the delegates of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Chiefs of Police, or the ASEANAPOL. The Philippines, through the PNP, is this year’s host of the five-day event which started on July 22. ASEANAPOL is a regional organization that brings together the national police forces of ASEAN member countries to share information, build skills, and fight cross-border crimes. Nartatez said the issue of school shootings cropped up during the discussion on peace order wherein the protection of children were cited, “The discussion was about transnational crime and it was mentioned because of the word children, minor, especially online cases against or exploitation against children.” “And that was the time when the idea of having a legislative agenda, effort to address it cropped up,” said Nartatez. The social media ban for minors would likely be recommended by the PNP to the Congress and Maj. Gen. Matthew Baccay, head of the Directorate for Investigation and Detective Management (DIDM), said the legislation could be patterned after that of Australia. “During one of the discussions, the influence of social media was discussed and it was also cited that there is an existing ban in Australia on the use of social media of a certain age in their population,” said Baccay. “It was agreed that perhaps we can borrow certain legislation to prevent the issue of social media and other platforms accessible to our children,’” he added.

Diokno gives chill response to Pia Cayetano’s 'Nagbabakasali lng' tirade. House prosecutor Akbayan Party-list Rep. Chel Diokno felt compelled on Saturday night, July 25 to post a correction to the Facebook video uploaded by Senator-judge Pia Cayetano regarding the recent oral arguments that took place during Vice President Sara Duterte's Senate impeachment trial. This was after House impeachment adviser and prosecution panel spokesperson Robert Ace Barbers aired his reservations about the video, which he described as "spliced" and "manipulated" . As expected, Diokno was very chill in his response--like the way he was during the oral arguments with Duterte's defense lawyer Michael Poa. The oral arguments concerned the prosecution panel's subpoena request for respondent Duterte's bank and tax records, as well as Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) reports. Presiding officer Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero ended up granting the prosecution’s request, despite the repeated insistence of the defense lawyers that the pursuit of the financial records was a "fishing expedition". But this didn't stop Pia Cayetano to lean into the defense's argument, as evidenced by her supplying the caption "Nagbabakasali lng? Walang mga ebidensya pero nag aakusa na! (Taking a chance? Accusing without evidence!)" to the subject Facebook clip. "With all due respect to the senator-judge at para hindi maligaw ang publiko, ito po ang konteksto at kumpleto na sinabi ko: '[Ang fishing expedition] ay maaaring sabihin nating nangyari kung only if the party requesting the evidence or documents ay nagbabakasakali lang, baka may makuha tayo dito,'” Diokno wrote. (With all due respect to the senator-judge and to avoid misleading the public, here is the context and the complete statement I made:‘[A fishing expedition] can be said to happen only if the party requesting the evidence or documents is merely taking a chance, hoping to find something.) At one point in the oral arguments, Pia Cayetano’s sibling, Senator-judge Alan Peter Cayetano, "debated" with Diokno on the fishing expedition argument. "Linawin ko po: Hindi tayo nagbabakasakali lang. May probable cause o sapat na dahilan na nakita sa mga record ng Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) tungkol sa bilyun-bilyong dumaan sa accounts ng VP at kanyang asawa," the lawyer-legislator underscored. (Let me clarify: We are not just taking a chance. There is probable cause or sufficient reason found in the records of the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) regarding billions that passed through the accounts of the Vice President and her husband.) The prosecution has said that the financial records were crucial to proving allegations of unexplained wealth against the Vice President. "Tandaan: Ang bank records ay maaari lang mailabas kapag may utos o subpoena mula sa korte. Ibig sabihin, kung nabuksan ng Kamara ang mismong bank records bago ang trial, paglabag yan sa karapatan at due process ni VP Sara Duterte," the soft-spoken Diokno said. (Remember: Bank records can only be released with a court order or subpoena. This means that if the House had opened the bank records before the trial, it would have violated the rights and due process of Vice President Sara Duterte.) Moving forward, Diokno said the senator-judges themselves would now be better aided in their decision-making regarding Duterte’s fate. "Ngayong may subpoena na para sa bank records ng Bise Presidente, magagamit ito ng magkabilang panig para patunayan ang kanilang kaso. Sa ganitong paraan, makakapagpasya ang mga senator-judges batay sa kabuuan ng ebidensya." (Now that there is a subpoena for the Vice President’s bank records, both sides can use them to prove their case.In this way, the Senator-Judges can decide based on the entirety of the evidence.)

On Our Radar eschelhaas Fri, 07/03/2026 - 19:07 Latest Updates Africa Asia-Pacific Europe Latin America & Caribbean Middle East & North Africa United States Global Issues & Institutions My Reading List Special Coverage / Global 03 July 2026 20+ minutes On Our Radar On Our Radar scans conflicts and crises around the globe every week and features some of the hotspots Crisis Group’s analysts are closely watching. Whether an under-reported trend or a headline-grabbing development, our field experts explain why it matters or what should be done. Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print 3 July 2026 AFGHANISTAN - PAKISTAN Tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan flared again this week. On Sunday, Pakistani forces once again carried out strikes across the border in Afghanistan, saying they killed 29 militants. Islamabad said the strikes were retaliation for recent attacks inside Pakistan, including a Karachi assault that killed three security personnel. According to the UN, at least 28 civilians were killed and another 49 injured in the strikes. Pakistan accuses the Afghan Taliban of sheltering anti-Pakistan militants, which Taliban officials deny. On Wednesday, Afghanistan said it carried out strikes inside Pakistan, targeting ISIS and other armed opposition groups. Islamabad denies Taliban accusations of harbouring such groups and noted that it had intercepted four drones launched from Afghan territory. Crisis Group expert Ibraheem Bahiss says outside mediators should push the sides toward practical border and security arrangements before the cycle of strikes and counterstrikes escalates further. NIGERIA Violence is again escalating in north-western Nigeria. Long plagued by bandits who engage in mass kidnappings for ransom, pillage and extortion, the region is also now seeing increased jihadist activity. Together, bandit and jihadist attacks killed over 150 people in Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara states in June, a notable uptick from previous months. On 28 May, Islamic State Sahel Province claimed what appears to be its first reported attacks in the region, in which eighteen soldiers and one police officer were killed in Kebbi and Sokoto states. Amid this escalation, on 20 June prominent bandit leader Bello Turji claimed responsibility for deadly attacks on troops and declared his group ready for either peace talks or prolonged war with the government. If the bandit and jihadist threats are not reined in, says Crisis Group expert Nnamdi Obasi, north-western Nigeria could become part of the wider belt of instability in the Sahel. SUDAN Fighting centred on El Obeid, North Kordofan’s state capital, has intensified in recent weeks as drone strikes increase and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) mobilise around the city, raising fears of encirclement and blockade. UN relief chief Tom Fletcher warned Tuesday that El Obeid risks becoming “another El Fasher”, referring to North Darfur’s capital, which endured a prolonged siege before falling to the RSF last October and suffering mass atrocities. Crisis Group expert Shewit Woldemichael says a siege of El Obeid would deepen the humanitarian crisis facing civilians, many of whom have already fled to the city from fighting elsewhere. Meanwhile, the increased use of drones against El Obeid could allow for sustained attacks through the now-beginning rainy season, when ground fighting has typically slowed. 26 June 2026 BOLIVIA President Rodrigo Paz declared a state of exception starting Saturday after more than 50 days of protests triggered by a land reform law and planned austerity measures. Authorities say at least 37 people have been injured in clashes between demonstrators and police. The decree bans the protesters’ roadblocks that have paralysed commercial traffic, causing shortages of basic goods in the administrative capital La Paz, and (temporarily) allows the armed forces to assist police in reopening key routes. It does not, however, suspend fundamental rights, as is often the case with states of exception in Latin America. Before making the declaration, Paz had signed an agreement to “pacify” the country with the biggest trade union, the Bolivian Workers’ Central, which withdrew from the streets. Most of the roadblocks have vanished since the measure took effect. But Crisis Group expert Glaeldys González Calanche says tensions remain high. The unrest could erupt anew if the government fails to deliver on socio-economic commitments it made to the union or if other groups involved in the protests, including campesinos and Indigenous people, decide to resume the pressure. COLOMBIA Right-wing Abelardo de la Espriella won Sunday’s presidential runoff by the thinnest margin in Colombian history, defeating Iván Cepeda, who had campaigned on continuing leftist President Gustavo Petro’s social reform agenda. De la Espriella styles himself as an outsider. Boasting of his ties to U.S. President Donald Trump, who endorsed him before the vote, he has vowed to take an iron-fist approach to organised crime, for instance pledging to bomb narco-traffickers and build mega-prisons. Many Colombians are ready for such measures, says Crisis Group expert Renata Segura, having become frustrated with Petro’s attempts to negotiate “total peace” with criminal and other armed groups. But, as the close vote shows, nearly half the electorate is equally concerned about de la Espriella’s promise to circumvent checks and balances in pursuit of quick fixes. To protect public safety, Colombia needs to balance crimefighting with efforts to plug the gaps in state services that criminal organisations exploit, including for recruitment. The new government should not disregard negotiations, which, if done the right way, have proven an effective tool for reducing violence in Colombia. U.S. - IRAN U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed Wednesday that technical delegations from the U.S. and Iran will reconvene at the end of June to resume talks aimed at ending the conflict between the two countries. By the terms of the memorandum of understanding reached between the Trump administration and Tehran in Islamabad earlier this month, these working groups are tasked with negotiating the details leading to a “final deal”, including nuclear commitments by Iran and sanctions relief provisions by the U.S. Maintaining momentum in dialogue is critical, says Crisis Group expert Ali Vaez, as the two sides have put forward clashing interpretations of the parameters they agreed to in Pakistan. The negotiations have many moving parts – related to the Strait of Hormuz and Lebanon, among other issues. In this ambitious scope lies promise, but also peril, as a setback on any one front could derail the whole endeavour. 19 June 2026 HAITI Visiting Tuesday, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said Haiti is suffering “the worst humanitarian crisis in the Western Hemisphere”. He toured the headquarters of the new Gang Suppression Force assembled to battle the criminal bands bedevilling the country. The UN released figures showing that gang violence has killed 2,300 people in the year to date and displaced a record 1.5 million more. Gangs have also kidnapped around 100 Haitians, including the defence ministry’s cabinet director last week. Crisis Group expert Diego Da Rin says much hope rests on the new force, but whether it can deliver remains to be seen as it builds toward its mandated strength of 5,500. Gangs, meanwhile, appear to be adapting, attacking senior officials and expanding abductions into formerly safe areas, possibly to deter anti-gang operations where kidnapping victims are held. MYANMAR - CHINA Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted Myanmar’s coup-leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing on a state visit to Beijing this week. The two sides reaffirmed their “community with a shared future” and signed eighteen agreements covering areas including transport and development. The visit highlighted Beijing’s priorities in Myanmar: border stability, protection of Chinese investment, progress on select China-Myanmar Economic Corridor projects and continued cooperation in combating online scams and other transnational crime. Crisis Group expert Richard Horsey says the state visit’s symbolism may matter more than any individual deal, as it provides Min Aung Hlaing with a measure of the international legitimacy he craves. For China, meanwhile, it is an opportunity to lock in a dependency that provides growing strategic opportunities, while it pushes for greater calm in conflict-affected areas along the Myanmar border. UKRAINE - RUSSIA Overnight into Thursday, Ukraine launched its largest drone assault on Moscow since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, hitting an oil refinery and injuring at least seventeen people. Russia said it intercepted 194 drones around Moscow and nearly 1,000 drones and several cruise missiles nationwide over 24 hours. Ukraine said the attack was a response to Russian strikes earlier this week that damaged the UNESCO-listed Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra monastery. Moscow warned it would respond forcefully. Crisis Group expert Lucian Kim says the attacks highlight Ukraine’s efforts to demonstrate it can hit targets far inside Russia using deep-strike drones. But while such attacks create headlines, they have yet to affect the Kremlin’s warfighting ability and may harden support for the war among the Russian public. 12 June 2026 AFGHANISTAN - PAKISTAN Pakistan launched air raids Wednesday across the border with Afghanistan, killing 26 Pakistani Taliban fighters, according to Pakistani Information Minister Attaullah Tarar. The Afghan authorities, however, said the strikes killed thirteen people, including eleven children. The air raids came one day after Pakistani Taliban fighters ambushed a security outpost in Pakistan’s north west, killing six officers. These incidents ended a month of calm in the conflict between the two countries. Crisis Group expert Ibraheem Bahiss says violent flare-ups like these are likely to persist as long as both countries’ security concerns remain unaddressed. IRAN - U.S. The fragile April ceasefire between Washington and Tehran wobbled as the two sides engaged in increasingly sharp exchanges of fire. U.S. forces launched repeated strikes on Iranian targets as Tehran retaliated by targeting U.S. bases in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait; Iran and Israel also traded blows for the first time in two months. On Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump threatened that the U.S. would take control of Kharg island, site of Iran’s main oil terminals, and other energy infrastructure. He backtracked later in the day, cancelling new strikes and insisting that a negotiated deal with Tehran was close. Crisis Group expert Ali Vaez says an agreement would be welcome if it steadies the shaky truce and gives Washington and Tehran a clear path to future negotiations. Those talks are likely to be fraught, however, and may not guarantee the end of hostilities if certain issues remain unresolved, such as Israel’s continued attacks on and occupation of over 20 per cent of Lebanon. WESTERN SAHARA A Moroccan airstrike on Sunday killed three Polisario Front members who were carrying out an attack on Moroccan fortifications in Western Sahara. Among the dead was Lehbib Mohamed Abdelaziz, son of Polisario’s former secretary general, who had been rumoured to be a candidate to become the Front’s leader. His death marks a major loss for the Polisario. The Moroccan strike came as UN envoy Staffan De Mistura was visiting the Tindouf refugee camps for consultations with the Polisario. Crisis Group expert Riccardo Fabiani says this latest episode shows that negotiations to resolve the Western Sahara conflict are under increasing strain. The Polisario and its ally Algeria have routinely rejected framework agreements based on Morocco’s autonomy plan as other deadly attacks have eroded trust between the parties. 5 June 2026 COLOMBIA Far-right presidential candidate Abelardo de la Espriella won a first-round victory in the 31 May elections, setting up a 21 June run-off against left-wing senator Iván Cepeda. Cepeda promises to reduce inequality and continue talks with armed groups, while de la Espriella advocates iron-fist policies, including bombing organised crime groups, building mega-jails and restoring traditional values. After the vote, President Gustavo Petro alleged irregularities, despite international observers calling the vote transparent, while U.S. President Donald Trump openly backed de la Espriella. Crisis Group expert Glaeldys González Calanche says Petro’s claims raise concerns over a peaceful transfer of power if Cepeda loses, while Trump’s involvement has fuelled resentment over foreign interference, which could further trigger demonstrations. The run-off could also test whether Trump’s endorsement helps or hurts candidates elsewhere in the region. CONFLICT-RELATED SEXUAL VIOLENCE The UN on 29 May released its annual report on conflict-related sexual violence, showing that reported cases more than doubled in 2025 after rising 25 per cent the year before. UN Women also recently reported that in Sudan alone, the number of women and girls needing support after sexual violence has quadrupled since civil war broke out three years ago. Crisis Group expert Cristal Downing says survivor services are increasingly scarce after major U.S. aid cuts in 2025 hit programming for which Washington had been the largest donor. Compounding the problem, Washington’s February 2026 “Protecting Human Flourishing in Foreign Assistance” policy restricts aid recipients’ work and speech on abortion. Though the policy’s ban on “promoting” abortion exempts cases of rape, many NGOs fear inconsistent enforcement and unclear compliance requirements, leaving them to choose between U.S. conditions that may limit post-rape care and refusing funding at the risk of jeopardising their wider operations. LEBANON Israel and Lebanon on Wednesday agreed to a new U.S.-brokered ceasefire deal, which would establish pilot zones in southern Lebanon where Hizbollah operatives would be barred. The deal follows a severe Israeli escalation, including its deepest incursion into Lebanese territory in 26 years, which threatened to upset ongoing U.S.-Iran talks. The ceasefire depends on Hizbollah halting attacks and withdrawing fighters from south of the Litani River to allow the Lebanese army to assume control there. On Thursday, Hizbollah rejected the terms, after Israel said it would continue military operations for now. Crisis Group expert David Wood says the “pilot zones” proposal could offer a pragmatic way to address the parties’ security concerns. Unless Israel and Hizbollah both cease fire, however, this latest agreement will soon collapse entirely. 29 May 2026 GAZA Nickolay Mladenov, the Bulgarian diplomat tasked by the U.S.-designed Board of Peace with overseeing the Gaza ceasefire, briefed the UN Security Council last week on his team’s first six months of work. He was upbeat, releasing a fifteen-point “roadmap” for the next stage. But conditions remain dire on the ground. Israel’s siege is tightening, meaning that reconstruction is impossible. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday he has ordered the Israeli army to increase the proportion of Gaza it controls from 60 to 70 per cent, in effect squeezing the strip’s two million people into an even tighter corner. Israeli airstrikes have taken more than 900 Palestinian lives during the ceasefire, including the commander of Hamas’s armed wing and, only days later, his successor, who was killed Wednesday along with his family. Israeli media reported that the Board of Peace had “approved” the assassinations. Crisis Group expert Max Rodenbeck says the Board’s strategy of making relief for Gaza’s people, whether humanitarian aid or broader hopes for the future, conditional on Hamas’s willingness to surrender its arms is deeply troubling and a recipe for prolonging their misery. KOREAN PENINSULA Pyongyang said it tested two new missiles Tuesday, including a short-range, nuclear-capable cruise missile that it plans to deploy with troops facing South Korean soldiers across the Korean peninsula’s demilitarised zone. The same day, Seoul said it had also detected North Korean missile launches toward waters off the peninsula’s western coast. Crisis Group expert Chris Green says the advanced weapon tests will deepen the freeze in peninsular relations, with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un branding South Korea his country’s foremost enemy and pledging to make the border “an impregnable fortress”. Along with Pyongyang’s growing closeness to Moscow and questions about Washington’s commitment to defending South Korea amid its mounting competition with Beijing, the tests are likely to bolster the consensus in Seoul behind more intensive military modernisation of its own. MALI As many as 50 people were killed Wednesday in jihadist raids on two villages in the central Mopti region, underscoring the breadth of the threat posed by the al-Qaeda affiliate Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM). Meanwhile, JNIM continued to enforce a partial siege of the capital Bamako, preventing scores of trucks bearing fuel and other supplies from reaching the city. In the north, Malian forces have stepped up airstrikes on Kidal and surrounding areas following the major offensive launched on 25 April by JNIM and northern separatist groups. Crisis Group expert Jean-Hervé Jezequel says these developments show that weapons continue to do the talking in Mali, even as the situation points to the urgent need for a genuine political dialogue. 22 May 2026 AFGHANISTAN Together with various NGOs, the UN released a plan Tuesday for aiding Afghan refugees expected to return from Iran and Pakistan in the coming months. The UN projects that 2.7 million people will cross back into Afghanistan between April and December. Already, nearly 5.9 million refugees have come back since September 2023, many of them forced to do so by harsh Pakistani visa policies amid rising tensions between Islamabad and the Taliban authorities in Kabul. Now the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran will likely compel many Afghans living in the Islamic Republic to leave, even as the exodus from Pakistan continues. Many of these people are women, who will face draconian Taliban restrictions on freedom of movement and economic activity. The returnees also include children, some of whom have never even been to Afghanistan and will be at greater risk of child marriage, which the Taliban have lately recognised as a legal act. Crisis Group expert Ibraheem Bahiss says international donors should give generously to fund the $529 million UN response plan, without which many returnees will be destitute. NIGERIA The military announced Tuesday that joint strikes carried out with the U.S. had killed 175 jihadist fighters in the preceding week, in addition to destroying stockpiles of arms. The strikes began on 16 May with one that killed Abu Bakr al-Mainuki, deputy leader of the Islamic State-West Africa Province (ISWAP), who had been coordinating activities with jihadists in the Sahelian countries. At a hearing in Washington on Tuesday, General Dagvin Anderson, head of U.S. Africa Command, told U.S. legislators that “the epicentre of global terrorism is in Africa”. Crisis Group expert Nnamdi Obasi says the latest operations underscore that Nigerian-U.S. security cooperation is deeper than Abuja and Washington had indicated earlier. They are a setback for ISWAP, at least for the time being. U.S. - CUBA The U.S. indicted former Cuban leader Raúl Castro Wednesday for murder and conspiring to kill U.S. nationals. The charges relate to a 1996 incident in which Cuban fighter jets shot at planes flown by anti-Castro Cuban Americans trying to help Cubans escape the island. These legal developments arrive amid renewed speculation that the Trump administration intends to decapitate the Cuban regime much as it did the Venezuelan government with its raid to snatch former President Nicolás Maduro in early January. Senior U.S. officials, most recently Central Intelligence Agency head John Ratcliffe, have held a series of semi-secret meetings with high-ranking figures in Havana this spring. Publicly, Cuban leader Miguel Díaz-Canel has remained defiant, rejecting the allegations against Castro as a “political manoeuvre”. Meanwhile, the U.S. has tightened a blockade of Cuba that has precipitated a humanitarian crisis and sent additional warships to the Caribbean Sea. Crisis Group expert Renata Segura says any attempt to forcibly break the tight grip the Cuban Communist Party and military have upon the state could result in violent chaos and further suffering for the Cuban people. 15 May 2026 DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO A spate of lethal violence in the north-eastern Ituri province over the past two weeks has underscored the complexity of the country’s crisis. In late April, a group of Codeco militiamen killed at least 69 people, mainly civilians, in a series of separate attacks. Allied with the Congolese government, Codeco claims to defend the interests of the Lendu people, most of whom are farmers, from encroachment by ethnic Hema herders. According to local sources, it raided several Hema villages in retaliation for assaults on Congolese army positions by a Hema armed group. The following week, gunmen from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan insurgency now affiliated with the Islamic State, killed at least fifteen people in Biakato, an Ituri market town. The province has been under martial law since 2021, the same year that Uganda (with Kinshasa’s permission) sent in troops to pursue ADF militants based in Congolese territory. Crisis Group expert Onesphore Sematumba says the latest killings demonstrate the inadequacy of a purely military response to insecurity stemming from inter-communal tensions, competition for natural resources, state weakness and other causes. DISPLACEMENT A new report from the Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre shows that armed conflict has become the number-one cause of internal displacement worldwide, surpassing natural disasters, for the first time on record. War and violence drove some 32.3 million people from their homes in 2025, the most ever, representing a 60 per cent increase over 2024. The internal displacements in Iran and the Democratic Republic of Congo made up two thirds of the global total. Crisis Group President and CEO Comfort Ero says these numbers are a sobering reminder of how pervasive conflict has become in today’s world. The human cost of war is never abstract. Preventing war means not just saving lives but also sparing people the pain and distress of being uprooted, often with no certainty of ever going home. U.S. - CHINA U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping concluded their long-awaited summit Friday. Crisis Group experts Ali Wyne and William Yang say it produced no major breakthrough, such as a joint commitment to de-escalate the conflict in the Middle East and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Nor did it bring a major reversal, which some in Taiwan had feared, such as Trump agreeing to scale back U.S. arms sales or change Washington’s longstanding declaratory policies toward the island. The summit was nonetheless illuminating in two respects. First, it underscored Trump’s desire to gain a greater foothold in China for U.S. businesses as well as his conviction that a strong working rapport with Xi can produce a cooperative relationship between Washington and Beijing. Secondly, it showcased how significantly China’s power and confidence have grown since Trump last visited China in November 2017. 8 May 2026 CAMBODIA - THAILAND The Thai cabinet voted Tuesday to cancel a 2001 memorandum of understanding with Cambodia on overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand. The agreement had provided for delimitation of maritime zones and joint development of hydrocarbon reserves in a portion of the 26,000 sq km overlapping claims area. Yet, in the 25 years since they signed it, the two countries have neither undertaken such projects nor resolved their territorial dispute. Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, who campaigned on scrapping the document arguing that it had failed to achieve its objectives, insists that the decision is unrelated to tensions with Cambodia following border clashes in 2025. Crisis Group expert Matt Wheeler says the cancellation will please Thai nationalists who have long alleged that the agreement placed Bangkok at a disadvantage, despite its language saying it is “without prejudice to the maritime claims of either party”. Cambodia expressed regret at Thailand’s action and said it plans to initiate compulsory conciliation, a non-binding dispute resolution mechanism under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. ETHIOPIA A showdown may be looming in Tigray, Ethiopia’s northernmost region, after its ruling party reinstated a state council Tuesday that was dissolved immediately before the bloody 2020-2022 Tigray war. The council was originally elected in 2020, in defiance of the federal government’s wishes. Addis Ababa installed a regional administration of its own choosing following the war, which Tigray’s ruling party has now, in effect, deposed. All eyes are now on the federal government, says Crisis Group expert Magnus Taylor, watching for how it will respond. It has already imposed what amounts to an economic siege on Tigray, blocking fuel supplies and withholding budget subsidies. It may simply tighten these measures. Or it may intervene militarily to reinstate an Addis Ababa-aligned administration. A new conflict in Tigray could drag in neighbouring countries, particularly Eritrea, adding to the turmoil in the Horn of Africa, as Addis Ababa and Asmara appear to be aligning with different sides in Sudan’s civil war. U.S. - CHINA Chinese leader Xi Jinping is due to host U.S. President Donald Trump in Beijing next week for a long-awaited summit, which had been slated for the end of March. Crisis Group experts Ali Wyne and William Yang say trade will likely feature high on the agenda, with both men aiming to maintain the tariff truce they reached last year. The Middle East conflict – which caused the delay – will also loom large, and both will seek to use it for leverage. The U.S. has sanctioned five Chinese oil refiners and accused China of “funding the largest state sponsor of terrorism” as it maintains a naval blockade of Iran. But Washington needs Chinese gallium to replenish its stockpile of missile interceptors in the Middle East, and it may need Beijing’s help to get Tehran back to the negotiating table. In exchange, Xi may try to extract security concessions from Trump, perhaps by asking him to lessen U.S. defence backing for Taiwan or to declare that the U.S. “opposes“ (rather than “does not support“, which is the longstanding U.S. position) Taiwanese independence. 1 May 2026 AFGHANISTAN - PAKISTAN Fresh violence between Afghanistan and Pakistan erupted this week. Afghan authorities said Pakistani mortars and missiles hit a university and residential neighbourhoods in eastern Kunar province on Monday, killing at least seven people and wounding at least 85. Pakistan denied targeting civilians, saying its strikes aimed at militants, based on intelligence. Pakistani officials accused Afghan forces of cross-border attacks as well, including mortar fire at Chaman and South Waziristan, which they said killed several civilians and injured others. The exchanges followed China-mediated talks in April, during which the two sides agreed to explore a diplomatic solution to their dispute. Crisis Group expert Ibraheem Bahiss says mutual partners, particularly China, should urge both sides to de-escalate tensions, including through an agreed-upon oversight mechanism, to prevent the situation from deteriorating further. COLOMBIA Nearly two dozen people are dead and scores injured after a series of apparently coordinated attacks in the country’s south west that authorities blamed on Estado Mayor Central (EMC), a dissident faction of the former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia. Militants used drones, explosives and roadblocks to hit targets including police stations and military bases. On 25 April, improvised explosive devices went off on a major highway in Cauca, striking a bus and other civilian vehicles, killing at least twenty. The preceding a day, a bus full of explosives detonated near a major military base in Cali, Colombia's third-largest city. Crisis Group expert Glaeldys González Calanche says the wave of violence indicates EMC’s capacity to disrupt daily life and terrorise civilians. Colombia's next president, to be elected on 31 May, will need to take urgent steps to better protect civilians. MALI On Saturday, the al-Qaeda affiliate Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, alongside separatists from the Azawad Liberation Front in northern Mali, assailed seven Malian cities, including the capital Bamako. Militants struck the garrison at Kati, less than 20km from Bamako, often described as the centre of military power, where they assassinated the defence minister and reportedly wounded other regime figures. They also retook the northern city of Kidal, the symbolic seat of the separatist movement, before negotiating the departure of Russian paramilitaries and Malian troops. Crisis Group expert Jean-Hervé Jézéquel says these attacks mark a new stage in Mali’s decades-long jihadist insurgency, characterised by increased pressure on urban areas, aimed at weakening and delegitimising state authority. 24 April 2026 JAPAN On Monday, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s cabinet lifted restrictions on the export of lethal weapons, allowing Japan to sell arms to seventeen countries with which it has defence transfer agreements. CATASTROFE IN EMILIA:ARRIVANO GLI AIUTI DALLA RUSSIA. La mobilitazione è stata rapidissima. Venerdì Putin ha chiamato l'amico Berlusconi, sabato pomeriggio il primo jet è decollato da una grande base alle porte di Mosca e nella serata è arrivato all'aeroporto militare a Pratica di Mare. Altri otto seguiranno nel giro di ore. Tutti i materiali raggiungeranno poi la l'Emilia Romagna e le zone colpite dalla grande alluvione. Le foto diffuse dal ministero della Difesa russo mostrano la colonna di mezzi che sale sui velivoli. Si notano alcuni camion militari, una fila di ufficiali e diversi furgoni con aiuti medici. Si contano anche 8 idrovore di ultima generazione, utilizzate per prosciugare il lago Bajkal. Il personale proviene dai ranghi della Protezione Civile, che fa capo al ministero dell’Interno, e da quelli delle forze armate. Dovrebbero essere parte delle unità pronte all’azione per fronteggiare le catastrofi e addestrate allo scenario della catastrofe alluvionale. E per questo in grado di operare con efficacia nella battaglia contro le acque.

MISTER FERGUSON SUL CASO JUVENTUS: "NELLA PREMIER VERREBBE RADIATA". ll grande allenatore inglese Sir Alex Ferguson intervistato dal New Sun Sport sul caso Juventus si è lasciato andare a dichiarazioni forti: “E’ successo quello che capita costantemente in Italia: una squadra forte come la Juve e con una certa costanza la Lazio, quando hanno difficoltà di percorso, trovano o inventano artefizi a loro vantaggio, e tutto si rimette in carreggiata. E’ sempre la stessa storia: gioiscono gli stessi e altri pagano dazio per farli gioire”. "La Juventus ha imbrogliato ed è stata sleale. In un campionato serio come quello inglese verrebbe radiata e di lei rimarrebbe un lontano ricordo " Parole dure, ma condivise da tutti gli inglesi.

CALABRIA: SALVIAMO LO SCOGLIO DEL DELFINO. Ad Africo(prov. di Reggio Calabria) e dintorni tutta la popolazione si sta mobilitando per salvare il famosissimo "Scoglio del Delfino" sita nelle mitiche scogliere di Africo. L'iniziativa è stata promossa dalle varie associazioni nazionali e internazionali affinché l'erosione calcarea e la stupidità d alcuni turisti non rovini questa meravigliosa forma d'arte scultorea che Madre Natura ci ha regalato. A causa di alcuni turisti col vizio di staccare, armati d martelletto, pezzi di roccia da portare a casa come souvenir, la parte anteriore dello Scoglio del Delfino è profondamente lesionata. E come se non bastasse, anche pescatori d frodo muniti di bombole e scalpello stanno minando le fondamenta a caccia di avalloni e datteri di mare. Per questo bisogna salvarla con un intervento di messa in sicurezza serio e risolutore.

WIJNALDUM COME PEDRO: DALLA ROMA ALLA LAZIO. TRATTATIVA IN FASE AVANZATA. Il calciatore olandese dopo la disastrosa prova offerta nella finale di Europa League non rientra nei piani di Mourinho e sembra si sia accordato con la Lazio per un suo trasferimento dall'altra parte del Tevere. Il trasferimento è a costo zero, la Roma non percerpirà nessun indenizzo da parte dei biancocelesti e risparmierà sull'ingaggio pesante del calciatore. Al PSG detentore del cartellino del calciatore andrà però un introito legato ai bonus di presenze o di raggiungimento di determinati obiettivi da parte del calciatore. Georgino Wijnaldum è in trattativa con la Lazio per un biennale da 3,5 milioni di euro e vestirà la maglia numero 30. Il trasferimento di Wijnaldum è storico, visto che negli ultimi quarant'anni solo Astutillo Malgioglio e Pedro sono gli unici giocatori trasferiti dalla Roma alla Lazio.

ORIGI, MESSIAS, ADLI E 25 MILIONI PER MILINKOVIC-SAVIC. LOTITO NE CHIEDE 35!!!. Il Milan, dopo lo scioccante siluramento di Paolo Maldini, punta al grande colpo per il calciomercato estivo: Sergej Milinkovic-Savic della Lazio . Lo ha riferito ' SportMediaset '. Il Diavolo, dunque, ha intenzione di andare all'assalto del centrocampista serbo, classe 1995 , che gioca nella Capitale dal 2015 e che ora sembra arrivato al momento dei saluti. Nonostante il contratto di Milinkovic-Savic scadrà tra un anno, il 30 giugno 2024 , il Presidente della Lazio, Claudio Lotito , continua a valutarlo molto. Si parla di 35-40 milioni di euro, per un giocatore che, in fin dei conti, in questa stagione con le Aquile di Maurizio Sarri si è riconfermato come uno dei centrocampisti più forti e completi del panorama calcistico mondiale. Motivo per cui il Milan, pur di metterlo a disposizione di Stefano Pioli in questo calciomercato estivo, sarebbe pronto ad offrire alla Lazio 25 milioni più ben tre contropartite tecniche individuati in Junior Messias , Divock Origi e Yacine Adli. Le contropartite tecniche sarebbero di gradimento per Mister Sarri e si adatterebbero facilmente al suo gioco spettacolare: Adli può ricoprire diversi ruoli del centrocampo e sarebbe un sostituto ideale del capitano biancoazzurro; Messias , visto il flop di Romero e l'età avanzata di Pedro, sarebbe un'ottima alternativa di fascia visto i tanti impegni che aspettano la Lazio; Origi sarebbe una discreta opzione a Ciro Immobile, lasciando crescere con tranquillità il talentuoso Cancellieri. La palla passa a Lotito che attende un rialzo di offerta magari intorno ai 30 milioni e l'inserimento di tre contropartite tecniche di buon livello per concludere l'affare.

TESSERA ONORARIA E MAGLIETTA RICORDO. I LAZIALI SCATENATI. Anthony Taylor socio onorario del Lazio Club. È questo il modo in cui tifosi biancocelesti del luogo hanno pensato di rifarsi contro la tifoseria romanista, dopo la “barbara aggressione dei sostenitori giallorossi” – come l’hanno definita loro – all’aeroporto di Budapest hanno pensato di esprimere la loro “vicinanza” all’arbitro inglese noto alle cronache per gli errori arbitrali durante la finale di Europa League. Così, il un articolo de ‘Il Messaggero’, il Lazio Club Pomezia ha deciso di staccare una tessera onoraria proprio a nome di Anthony Taylor, il fischietto che ha danneggiato la Roma in finale di Europa League scatenando le proteste e l’amarezza di Mourinho e i romanisti. LAZIO: NON SOLO BERARDI, ECCO HAZARD!!!. Nonostante una campionato giocato ad alti livelli, i limiti della rosa (specialmente in termini numerici) sono stati evidenti. Questo è ciò a cui la Lazio , a detta di Sarri stesso, deve puntare nelle prossime stagioni. Giocatori forti e pronti: questo l'identikit tracciato da Sarri per il mercato ormai alle porte. Seguito con grande interesse c'è Domenico Berardi che, dopo l'ultima partita stagionale ha parlato di Champions come obiettivo. E' stata messa sul tavolo un'offerta da 20 milioni più il cartellino di Matteo Cancellieri. Ma Lotito è scatenato e vuole regalare alla piazza biancoceleste un grande colpo. Il giocatore sarebbe contento di trasferirsi nella capitale e su questa base è stata avviata una trattativa, magari inserendo il Sergente.

CONFERENCE LEAGUE :POSSIBILE 0-3 A TAVOLINO PER LA FIORENTINA. I TIFOSI VIOLA CI SPERANO!!!. Gli otto punti rimediati da Cristiano Biraghi in finale di Conference League contro il West Ham hanno fatto molto discutere, non soltanto per il gesto vergognoso. Tra le questioni affrontate anche quella dell’interruzione della partita e del 3-0 a tavolino, provvedimenti su cui l’arbitro Del Cerro Grande, da norma, non può nulla. È la Commissione Disciplinare Uefa a decidere. Andiamo quindi a spulciare il regolamento. Tra i casi in cui i club devono rispondere delle azioni della tifoseria c’è anche “il lancio di oggetti che possa mettere in pericolo l’integrità fisica di altri presenti alla partita o pregiudicarne lo svolgimento”. Il paradosso è che Biraghi, per sperare in un 3-0 a tavolino, avrebbe dovuto accentuare il dolore e farsi sostituire, invece è stato “colpevole” di essersi grintosamente rialzato. Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

TUTTI PAZZI PER GEDSON FERNANDES. ECCO CHI E' TALENTO SULLA CIMA DEI DESIDERI DI MISTER SARRI. Uno dei nomi caldi per il centrocampo della Lazio è quello di Gedson Fernandes del Besiktas . Il portoghese classe 1999 ma nato nella Repubblica Democratica di São Tomé e Príncipe in Africa , piace tantissimo al tecnico biancoceleste Sarri che sembra lo abbia messo in cima alla liste delle priorità per il centrocampo. "Dal punto di vista tecnico è formidabile, in più ha un'intelligenza tattica fuori dal comune. Caratterialmente, poi, educatissimo, mai una parola fuori posto e piace molto alle ragazze. In poche parole, un predestinato per eccellenza. Con mister Sarri può diventare tra i cinque centrocampisti più forti al mondo se capirà il calcio italiano" Queste le parole di Senol Gunes allenatore del Besiktas, grande amico di mister Sarri e noto simpatizzante laziale.

MISTER SARRI: VOGLIO BOLOCA. Fino a qualche tempo fa lo conoscevano in pochi. Ora però il nome di Daniel Boloca inizia a circolare insistentemente anche tra i club di Serie A. Merito di una stagione strepitosa con il Frosinone : il mediano classe 1998 è tra i protagonisti della promozione dei canarini. Grosso non ha mai rinunciato a lui, mandandolo in campo con grande continuità. Al termine della stagione il bilancio è di 31 presenze (di cui 29 da titolare) e 2 gol all'attivo. La nostra testata ha intervistato in esclusiva Giorgio Boscarato , agente FIFA che lo ha seguito agli inizi della carriera e ci ha detto di lui: "Daniel secondo me è pronto per la Serie A, magari subito in una big, e con un club che possa valorizzarlo sono convinto che nel giro di un anno possa arrivare la chiamata in Nazionale. Non dimentichiamo che è un grande rubacuori e ad ogni fine allenamento posa per decine e decine di selfie per le tante ragazze che vengono a salutarlo".

Il Milan cerca rinforzi e, viste le ristrettezze finanziarie con cui è costretto a fare i conti da qualche tempo a questa parte, poter inserire un giocatore come il nazionale tedesco appare prospettiva allettante. In uno scenario il Milan , interessato da tempo al tedesco, ha già anticipato tutti proponendo un triennale, ma occhio a Mourinho pronto a convincere il giocatore con cui c'è un ottimo feeeling.

LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

THEBORDELINE, PUTIN: "QUATTRO MOCCIOSI SENZA CERVELLO.VI MANDEREI IN SIBERIA!. Vladimir Putin si è scagliato contro i TheBorderline . Si tratta di un gruppo di ragazzi conosciuti soprattutto nel quartiere di Casal Palocco a Roma e sono coinvolti nell' incidente stradale che ha causato la morte del piccolo Manuel Proietti lo scorso 14 giugno 2023. Uno di loro, Matteo Di Pietro , è indagato per omicidio stradale poiché al volante della Lamborghini che ha distrutto la Smart Forfour in cui era il bambino di 5 anni con la sua mamma e la sua sorellina. Il dittatore russo si è rivolto contro i ragazzi che hanno un seguito di oltre 600mila utenti. «Vi odio profondamente. Buttate la chiave della cella», ha detto Putin. Il premier si è sfogato durante una conference call con il premier indiano Modi contro gli youtuber: «Quattro mocciosi viziati e senza cervello noleggiano un'auto di lusso con i soldi di papino e distruggono una famiglia. Li manderei in Siberia a scavare carbone. Inutili ».

L'INTER ESERCITA IL DIRITTO DI RISCATTO PER ACERBI. ALLA LAZIO 4 MILIONI DI EURO. Francesco Acerbi e l'Inter. Il matrimonio proseguirà.
